Who sends the Pierce County tax bill

Pierce County combines valuing and collecting in a single Assessor-Treasurer's Office, so your assessment notice and your payment both go through the same door. Go to 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. To hand over a payment, Pierce County Finance, 1501 Market St., Suite 120, is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

  • Assessment and tax questions: (253) 798-6111.
  • Automated payment and balance line: (253) 798-3333. Have your parcel number ready.
  • Mail a check made out to Pierce County to Pierce County Finance, P.O. Box 11621, Tacoma, WA 98411-6621, enclosing the remittance stub or writing the parcel number on it.
  • An outside vendor processes card and e-check payments and charges extra: 2.35% on credit cards, $0.50 per e-check and $3.50 per debit card.

Pierce County housing at a glance

Tacoma anchors the county, which had about 946,288 residents in July 2025, behind only King County. Puyallup, Lakewood, University Place, Gig Harbor, Bonney Lake and Sumner are among the cities, and parts of Auburn, Enumclaw, Milton and Pacific reach in as well. One county office bills a house in any of them.

Homeownership sits at 64.7%, across 382,172 housing units. Median value of an owner-occupied home is $526,600 and median household income is $99,564. About a quarter of workers commute to King County, which keeps demand tied to the wider Puget Sound market.

Due dates and late charges

The bill is paid in two halves, by April 30 and by October 31. The county shifts a weekend deadline to the following Monday, which happened with October 31 in 2026. Anyone still owing the second half should phone the office for an exact balance that includes interest.

Splitting the bill is a right only when it totals $50 or more. Under RCW 84.56.020, interest on late tax is worked out monthly. A home with one to four units pays 0.75% a month (9% a year) on the full year's tax beginning May 1, and no penalties apply. Bigger apartment buildings and personal property pay 1% a month and penalties on top.

DateWhat happens
April 30First half is due.
May 1Interest starts on the full-year tax if the first half is unpaid: 0.75% per month on homes of one to four units for tax year 2023 and later, 1% per month on other property.
June 1Three percent penalty on other property.
October 31 (moves to Monday if a weekend)Second half is due.
December 1Additional eight percent penalty on other property, for an 11% total.

If no statement reaches you by March 31 and a mortgage company does not pay your taxes, call (253) 798-6111 for a copy.

How the county values your house

Each year, every property is valued at 100% of true and fair market value, which means what a willing buyer would pay a willing seller. Assessed values track the market in both directions. Neighborhood desirability, building costs and improvements you have made all feed into the number.

A revaluation plan approved by the Washington Department of Revenue calls for a visit about every six years. Visits can happen sooner after new construction, a board case, an appraisal review, a sales verification or a split of the parcel. You may refuse private access, but not to the assessor or staff. To confirm a staff member's credentials, call (253) 798-6111.

Countywide, taxes total almost $2.1 billion, paying for schools, libraries, parks and emergency services.

How to appeal your Pierce County assessment

Your appeal goes to the Pierce County Board of Equalization. You can file up to July 1 of the assessment year, or up to 60 days after a value change notice was mailed, if that gives more time. For the form, call (253) 798-7415. RCW 84.40.038 also lets a board excuse a late filing for good cause.

You need specific reasons why the assessor's number differs from market value (RCW 84.40.0301). The size of the increase, personal hardship, the amount of the tax and anything unrelated to market value cannot be weighed. Reasons that count as good cause:

  • A death or serious illness affecting you or close family.
  • Incorrect written filing advice from board or assessor staff.
  • A flood, earthquake or similar disaster.
  • A mail delay the Postal Service has documented.

Missed July 1? A notice mailed in the last 60 days may still leave you time.

Senior and disability tax relief

The county offers an exemption that lowers the tax and a deferral that postpones it. Eligibility for the exemption is widening. From January 2027, bills drop for more homeowners who are 61 or older or have a qualifying disability. The new tier requires:

  • You owned and lived in the home at least six months in 2026.
  • You turned 61 in 2026, or you are a veteran with at least a 40% disability rating, or a taxpayer with a qualifying disability who did not serve.
  • Combined household income is $85,000 or less for 2026, with a standard deduction for items such as medical premiums and prescription drugs.

Owners who met the earlier rules in 2023, 2024 or 2025 can still apply and could receive a refund. For those years the limit was income up to $64,000 and a veteran rating of at least 80%.

The deferral is a different animal. Reapply each year. You need to be 60 or older on December 31 of the year you apply, with yearly income under $68,319. The state's Department of Revenue pays the county on your behalf, and what it pays becomes a lien that you repay with interest when the home changes hands (RCW 84.38).

Property tax when you sell a Pierce County house

A new tax lien attaches to the parcel every January 1. When your contract has no proration clause, RCW 84.60.020 puts the pre-closing part of the year on you and the rest on the buyer. The escrow officer usually figures the split and subtracts any unpaid balance, interest or deferral from your proceeds. Line up a payoff figure before you take an offer.

Sellers usually owe the state real estate excise tax too, payable to the county treasurer as of the sale date. For closings on or after January 1, 2027, the state charges 1.1% on the first $551,000, 1.28% on the next slice up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000 and 3% on everything above, plus the local share.

A move need not end a senior exemption. RCW 84.36.381 allows a claimant who sells or is displaced to carry exemption status to a replacement residence, though only one home a year can have it.

If you are behind on Pierce County property taxes

Losing a house to unpaid tax takes years. A certificate of delinquency cannot issue under RCW 84.64.050 until three years after the delinquency date, and none can be filed for $100 or less. Owners and holders of recorded interests are notified and given thirty days to appear or pay.

Several choices come first. A payment agreement or partial payments may be available from the treasurer. As the three-year mark approaches, the treasurer must waive outstanding interest and penalties for an owner with limited income who lives in the home and never got a waiver before (RCW 84.56.020). Payments aimed at avoiding foreclosure go to the Assessor-Treasurer's Office, Attention: Foreclosure Avoidance, 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, WA 98409-1498.

When back taxes make keeping the house impractical, request a payoff figure from the treasurer and let your escrow officer settle it from the sale proceeds. A cash buyer can shorten the timeline, since no lender review is involved.

Frequently asked questions

When is the second half of Pierce County property tax due?

It is due October 31, or the following Monday when that date is a weekend, as it was in 2026. For a balance with interest on anything unpaid, call (253) 798-6111.

Who do I call about my Pierce County assessment?

Dial (253) 798-6111 for the Assessor-Treasurer's Office. The Board of Equalization, which supplies appeal forms, is at (253) 798-7415.

Can I still appeal if July 1 has gone by?

Often. With a value change notice, the deadline is the later of July 1 and 60 days after mailing. Boards can also take a late petition for good cause.

Does the senior exemption follow me to a new home?

Frequently. RCW 84.36.381 lets someone who sells or is displaced transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, up to one exempt home a year.

Who pays the property tax at closing in Pierce County?

Your contract controls. When it says nothing, the seller owes taxes up to the day before the sale and the buyer owes the remainder, and escrow does the math.

King County context for sellers

King County is Washington's most populous county, with Seattle as seat and largest city. Residents numbered 2,269,675 in 2020 and about 2,344,939 in 2025. Cities from Seattle and Bellevue to Kent, Renton, Redmond, Kirkland, Federal Way, Sammamish, Issaquah, Enumclaw, Snoqualmie and North Bend all sit inside the county, plus part of Auburn. Which city and special districts cover your parcel decides the levies on your bill, so two similar houses can carry quite different totals.

Who to call about your King County bill

Three separate county bodies touch your bill. The Department of Assessments sets values, Treasury Operations bills and collects, and the Board of Appeals and Equalization hears valuation disputes. The Board is an independent agency, not a branch of the assessor's office.

OfficeWhat it handlesPhone
Department of AssessmentsValues, parcel records, general questions206-296-7300
Assessments, senior exemptionsSenior and disability relief206-296-3920
King County Tax AdvisorAdvice on property tax matters, including appeals206-477-1060
Board of Appeals and EqualizationValuation appeals206-477-3400
Treasury Operations hotlinePayments, statements, account status206-263-2890
Treasury foreclosure unitParcels in or near tax foreclosure206-263-2649

Treasury is at 201 S. Jackson St., Suite 710, in Seattle's Pioneer Square. The Customer Service Center on the second floor takes in-person payments on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Why 2026 bills rose

Countywide, 2026 property taxes total $8.4 billion, roughly $770 million or 10% above the $7.7 billion of the year before. Taxable value grew only about 5.4%, from $873 billion to $920 billion, so bills outran values.

Most of the jump traces to measures voters approved, not to rising property values. The county government keeps about 20% of what is collected, spending it on roads, criminal justice and public health. State government, cities, schools and other districts split the rest.

Voters approved these measures for 2026:

  • Seattle: a six-year renewal levy for families, education and preschool, plus a ten-year lid lift for election vouchers.
  • Bothell: a ten-year renewal of the Safe Streets and Sidewalks lid lift.
  • Mercer Island: a $103,160,000 general obligation bond for a new facility.
  • School District 1: replacement capital and education and operations levies.
  • King County: a six-year parks, recreation, trails and open space levy.

Before you price your house, search the parcel in the Assessor's eReal Property tool. It shows valuation, levy rates and sale history.

Due dates and late charges

You owe the first half by April 30 and the second by October 31. When either date lands on a weekend or county holiday, the deadline becomes the next business day. The only mailing is a statement in mid-February. After that you hear nothing unless you request reminders, which the Treasury site offers by text or email.

If April 30 passes unpaid, the entire year becomes delinquent on May 1 and late charges are computed monthly on the full-year amount. You may still pay the first half plus charges before October 31. Miss the second half and monthly charges begin November 1 on that portion. The county points out that state law gives it no power to grant extensions, whatever the reason.

A check by mail or at the counter costs nothing extra. Online, the card fee is 2.35% of the charge with a $2 minimum, and an eCheck is a flat $0.55. If a lender pays from escrow, it usually sends one bulk payment close to the deadline. Contact the lender if your parcel still shows unpaid ten days after the due date.

Think a tax is unlawful or excessive and want to keep the right to sue for a refund? Hand in a separate written statement when you pay, saying you pay under protest and listing every reason.

How to appeal a King County valuation

Once you get a valuation notice, you can contest it with the Board of Appeals and Equalization. Petitions go in through the eAppeals portal, or by mail on forms you download.

The filing window comes from RCW 84.40.038. Whichever falls last controls: July 1 of the assessment year, 30 days after the notice, or a period of up to 60 days where the county legislative authority has set one. Your notice prints the date that applies to you, and the board will clarify at 206-477-3400. Missing it is not always fatal. The board can excuse a late petition for good cause, for instance a family death, serious illness or a documented mail delay.

Appeals turn on market evidence. Collect any of these:

  • Recent sales of comparable homes near yours.
  • A contractor's estimate for defects the assessor has not accounted for.
  • An independent appraisal.
  • Photos and records that expose a wrong lot size, bedroom count or square footage.

Separately, the Assessor takes petitions for a refund when a manifest error in the property description, such as wrong square footage, was used to set value. The look-back can reach six years, depending on the evidence.

Help for King County owners

The county's reduction program is for owner-occupants aged 61 and over, or retired on disability, with income below the state limit. Apply at TaxRelief.kingcounty.gov or call 206-296-3920. It covers one residence and up to one acre. In a multi-family building, the owner's own unit is the only part that counts. Deferral of taxes is available under certain conditions.

Two other programs matter if you renovate or sell. Adding rooms, a deck or a patio to a single-family home may earn a three-year exemption on the improvement's value, but you must apply before construction is finished. Damaged or destroyed property can qualify for a lower assessed value, and the Assessor's office takes those questions at 206-263-2332.

What you owe at closing

Sellers normally cover Washington's real estate excise tax, and the amount tracks the sale price. The county treasurer is owed the money as of the day of sale, even if recording happens later. A month of delay brings penalties and interest. Should the seller fail to pay, responsibility shifts to the buyer and the tax can attach to the property as a lien.

Washington's state share climbs in steps. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 are taxed by the Department of Revenue at 1.1% on the first $551,000, 1.28% up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000, and 3% beyond. Your city's local rate is extra. Treasury or your closing agent can quote the total.

Read the tax statement for non-tax charges too. These vary by location and include surface water management, City of Seattle drainage, fire protection, King Conservation District and noxious weed fees. If a new house or addition was never assessed, an omit tax can reach back up to three years and is billed with an extra year to pay.

Can you sell a King County house that is behind on taxes?

Yes. Late charges on a delinquent parcel grow each month, though, so request a current payoff figure from Treasury before you fix a closing date. Call the hotline at 206-263-2890. For any parcel in foreclosure use 206-263-2649, because foreclosure costs are added and cannot be paid online.

Payment plans exist for past due prior-year taxes. A plan lasts no more than 12 months, late charges are not reduced, each plan carries a one-time $100 setup fee, and a vendor adds a monthly processing fee. Taxes three years or more past due can go to foreclosure. An owner who lives in the home and has limited income can request a waiver of interest and penalties as that three-year mark nears, as RCW 84.56.020 describes.

If time is the problem, a direct sale to a cash buyer may close before the tax situation worsens. Weigh it against a regular listing and against a payment plan.

Frequently asked questions

When are King County property taxes due?

The first half is due April 30 and the second October 31. A weekend date, like October 31 in 2026, moves to the next business day. After that, unpaid tax collects monthly late charges.

Where do I file a King County valuation appeal?

With the Board of Appeals and Equalization, online through eAppeals or by mail. It is separate from the Assessor and answers at 206-477-3400.

Who pays real estate excise tax when I sell in King County?

The seller, in most sales. It is owed to the county treasurer when the sale occurs. Price sets the state rate, a local rate is added, and Treasury or your closing agent can give the total.

Can seniors lower their King County property tax?

Often, yes. Occupant-owners who are 61 or older, or retired due to disability, may qualify with income under the state limit. Apply at TaxRelief.kingcounty.gov or call 206-296-3920.

Does King County offer a payment plan for back taxes?

Yes, for prior-year taxes that are past due. Plans run up to 12 months, late charges still apply, and there is a one-time $100 setup fee per plan. Call 206-263-2649 or email PaymentPlans@kingcounty.gov.

Skagit County at a glance

Skagit County covers about 1,730 square miles of the Puget Sound region and holds 132,975 people. Its seat and biggest city is Mount Vernon. Property types vary widely: the Skagit River valley is tulip, blueberry and strawberry country, Fidalgo and Guemes islands have shoreline lots, and the east side climbs into the Cascade foothills.

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $545,100, and owners live in 70.1% of housing units. With 25.0% of residents at least 65 years old, the senior exemption described below matters to a lot of local owners.

Who handles property tax

The Assessor decides values, sets levies and approves exemptions. The Treasurer mails bills and takes payments. A separate Board of Equalization hears disputes over value.

OfficeResponsibilityContact
TreasurerCollects tax, accepts payments, handles late-payment questions700 S. 2nd Street, Room 205, Mount Vernon, WA 98273; 360-416-1750; mail to PO Box 518
AssessorValues property, sets levies, approves exemptions360-416-1780; assessor@skagitcountywa.gov
Board of EqualizationHears assessed value appeals700 S. 2nd Street, Room 100, Mount Vernon; clerk at 360-416-1126

If Mount Vernon is a long drive, the Concrete satellite office at 45770 A Main Street takes cash, check or money order.

Due dates and how to pay

The yearly tax splits into halves due April 30 and October 31. A bill under $50 is paid whole by April 30 (RCW 84.56.020). The next date to remember is April 30, 2027.

Options for paying:

  • Visit the Treasurer in Mount Vernon with cash, a check, a money order or a card.
  • Leave a check or money order in a drop box at 700 S. 2nd Street, either by the west end of the horseshoe parking lot or upstairs outside Room 205.
  • Call 1-866-791-3392. The processor charges $3.95 plus 2.35% on debit and credit cards, or $1.00 on checks.
  • Enroll in auto-pay, which draws from a U.S. checking or savings account on April 30 and October 31, or takes the whole year on April 30. Forms are due April 15 for spring and October 15 for fall.

Envelopes are risky. The Postal Service no longer promises a same-day postmark, and a late postmark means a late payment. Mail early or use a drop box.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Skagit County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What late payment costs

Interest starts May 1 and is charged on the entire year's tax, not just the missed half. Call the Treasurer, 360-416-1750, for the exact amount to send.

State law (RCW 84.56.020) treats homes differently from other property for taxes levied from 2023 on. A residence with up to four units, or a manufactured home, owes 9% a year and no penalty. Commercial and personal property owe 12% a year, plus penalties of 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

Forgiveness is limited. If the county never mailed your notice, the treasurer has to drop interest and penalties. A death in the family, of a spouse or of a parent or stepparent, can excuse one missed payment on a personal residence, but only if you tell the treasurer within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). The office also arranges payment plans and takes partial payments, crediting the oldest year first.

How to appeal your assessment

File with the Skagit County Board of Equalization by the date on your Notice of Value. The statute (RCW 84.40.038) sets July 1 or 30 days from mailing, whichever is later. Even owners with an unchanged value, and no notice, face the same cutoff.

Missed it? The board may still take a petition filed within a reasonable time if you show good cause, such as a serious illness or a postal delay documented by the Postal Service. The clerk, at 360-416-1126, can tell you whether you qualify.

Hearing basics:

  • Ten minutes for you, ten for the Assessor, then your reply.
  • The Assessor's value is presumed right, so you carry the burden of proving an error with clear, cogent and convincing evidence (RCW 84.40.0301).
  • What works: sales of comparable houses near the valuation date, contractor repair bids and independent appraisals. What does not: asking prices.
  • Additional documents are due 21 business days ahead.
  • Expect the process to take 6 to 12 months.

The board will not consider the size of your bill, hardship or how big the increase was. A losing owner can take the case to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days.

Senior and disability exemption

Skagit's main relief program serves owners 61 or older, owners with disabilities and owners with a 40% VA disability rating. The income ceiling rises to $78,000 in 2027.

To qualify, add up disposable income for everyone who owns and lives in the home: adjusted gross income plus untaxed items such as Social Security, pensions and annuities. Then subtract either $7,500 per person (you and a spouse or domestic partner) or your real qualifying costs, such as prescriptions, Medicare premiums and care. Beginning in 2027 you may also subtract up to $6,000 of rent collected from living space in your home. The Assessor, at 360-416-1780, will walk through the worksheet with you.

If a fire or similar event destroys part of a property, you have three years to claim a value reduction (RCW 84.70.010). The state also runs a deferral program for eligible owners, which the Assessor can explain.

Special charges on the bill

Some charges are special assessments that fall outside the 1% cap on regular levies. The Assessor does not set them. Each district or program writes its own budget and divides it by acreage, value or some other formula.

  • Diking and drainage districts look after dikes, ditches and pump stations in their areas.
  • The Clean Water Assessment supports the county's Clean Water Program, aimed at bacterial pollution, including Samish Bay shellfish beds, along with septic repairs and water monitoring.
  • The County Drainage Utility pays for pump stations, piping, tide gates, ditches and similar stormwater work.

Two homes assessed at the same value can still owe different totals, because each belongs to its own mix of city, school, fire and library districts.

Selling with taxes owed

Back taxes on the parcel come out of your sale proceeds, or the buyer inherits them. Before accepting an offer, ask the Treasurer for a payoff that covers each unpaid year.

Selling also brings real estate excise tax. It is owed to the county treasurer on the sale day and is usually the seller's cost. For sales from January 1, 2027, the state steps run 1.1% to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above, with a local rate on top. The Treasurer can quote the total.

Do not let the debt age: foreclosure starts by law after three years (RCW 84.64.050). Owners who live in the home and meet income limits may get interest and penalties waived shortly before then (RCW 84.56.020).

With cash, no lender holds up closing, and the title company settles with the Treasurer from your proceeds. Either way, get the payoff on paper first.

Frequently asked questions

When are Skagit County property taxes due?

Two halves, April 30 and October 31, unless the bill is under $50, in which case all of it is due April 30. Next is April 30, 2027. Interest begins the day after a missed spring due date.

Can I still appeal my Skagit County value?

Check the date on your Notice of Value. After it, the board may still take a petition for good cause, such as serious illness or a documented postal delay. Call the clerk, 360-416-1126, with your parcel number.

What interest rate applies to late Skagit County tax?

Houses with up to four units pay 9% a year, no penalty. Other property pays 12% plus penalties of 3% and then 8%. Phone the Treasurer, 360-416-1750, for your parcel's exact payoff.

Who do I call about a Skagit County property tax question?

Use the Treasurer, 360-416-1750, for bills, payments and payoffs. Use the Assessor, 360-416-1780, for values and exemptions. The Board of Equalization clerk, 360-416-1126, handles appeals.

How long can Skagit County property tax stay unpaid before foreclosure?

Three years past delinquency, the treasurer must begin foreclosure. No certificate can be filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less (RCW 84.64.050). Pay or sell well before then, since interest grows each month.

Snohomish County at a glance

Snohomish County lies on Puget Sound north of Seattle, and Everett is both its seat and its largest city. It is Washington's third most populous county, at 870,656 people over about 2,087 square miles. Most of those people live on the Sound side, while the eastern half climbs into the Cascades and is mostly national forest.

The median value of an owned home is $696,000, and 68.2% of homes are owner-occupied. Farmed river valleys such as the Stillaguamish and the Snohomish flood now and then in big storms, so a low-lying parcel deserves a second look.

Which offices to call

Your Assessor sets values. Districts and voters set the levy, and the Treasurer turns both into your bill. Value disputes belong to a separate Board of Equalization.

  • Assessor: main line 425-388-3433, residential appraisal 425-388-6555, commercial 425-388-3390, exemptions 425-388-3540.
  • Treasurer: 425-388-3366, plus card payments by phone at 833-440-3332.
  • Board of Equalization: 425-388-3407, BOE@snoco.org, 3000 Rockefeller Ave m/s 409, Everett, WA 98201.

April 30First half due; personal property listings due
July 1Appeal petition deadline, depending on when your notice was mailed
July 15Board of Equalization meets in open session
October 31Second half due

Due dates and paying by mail or online

Half the tax, or all of it, is due April 30, with the other half due October 31. A bill under $50 is paid in one piece in April. Your next deadline is April 30, 2027.

A mailed payment needs a postmark by the due date, and an online one must be completed by then, or the tax is delinquent. The Postal Service changed how it postmarks, so the Treasurer advises mailing several days ahead, getting a hand-stamped postmark or using certified mail. Allow a week or more for a mailed check to clear. A drop box on the county campus takes checks around the clock, but do not use the ballot box for tax payments.

For a sale, phone the Treasurer at 425-388-3366 well before closing.

What happens when you pay late

Skip the April 30 half and the entire year's tax goes delinquent, with charges figured on all of it. Those charges are added on the first of each month.

Under RCW 84.56.020 the rate depends on property type. A house of up to four units, or a manufactured home, taxed in 2023 or later accrues 9% a year with no penalty. Anything else, personal property included, accrues 12% and picks up a 3% penalty after June 1 and 8% more after December 1.

Waivers are uncommon. A county error that kept the notice from reaching you can qualify. So can the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent behind a missed residence payment, provided the treasurer hears from you within 60 days (RCW 84.56.025). Payment agreements and partial payments are also possible, credited oldest year first.

How your home's value is set

Washington requires assessment at full market value as of January 1. The county moved to yearly reappraisal of every parcel with the 2004 assessment, abandoning the four-year cycle, so values track the market in both directions.

Think of your tax as a slice of the districts' total levy. The Assessor's number sets your slice. Budgets and voter-approved levies set the size of the pie, and regular levies cannot grow more than 1% a year without a public vote. A bigger value therefore does not always bring a bill that grows by the same percentage.

The system lags the market: this year's sales set next January's value, and the tax follows a year after.

How to appeal your assessment

To dispute a value, petition the Board of Equalization. The clock is 60 days from the date on your Notice of Value, or July 1 of the assessment year if you never got a notice, whichever falls later. That is the longest limit the state lets a county choose, and Snohomish County chose it. No fee applies, but each parcel needs its own petition.

  • File online before 4:00 PM on the last day, or send or bring a paper copy.
  • You receive a case number while the Assessor reviews the petition. If the two of you settle on a number, a signed stipulation closes the case.
  • No deal means a hearing roughly 60 days later, on Zoom unless you tell the clerk a week ahead that you want to appear in person.
  • Evidence goes to the board and the Assessor 21 business days before the hearing, up to 75 pages, with no audio, video or web links.
  • Expect the decision in the mail within 45 calendar days.

You carry the burden. The Assessor's number is presumed right, and RCW 84.40.0301 requires clear, cogent and convincing proof of a mistake. Listing prices, what you can afford and how much the bill jumped are not grounds. Stronger material includes sales of similar homes near January 1, a wrong square footage in the property record and contractor bids for major repairs. Both sides may appeal the ruling to the State Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days, and it covers only the year in question.

Senior and disability relief

A senior citizen and disabled person exemption is available through the Assessor. The income ceiling stood at $75,000 as of 2024, so call 425-388-3540 or email assessor@snoco.org for today's limit, and use the county's status tool to track your application.

Participants pay on the lower of the value frozen when they qualified or the current market value. Eligible seniors and disabled owners can also defer tax through a state program, but deferred tax is a lien and comes due when ownership transfers, which matters if you are selling.

Historic property and open space programs have their own application dates, so ask the Assessor if either could apply to your land.

Selling with taxes owed

If the house owes tax, the balance is paid at the sale. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that spans each year owed. Interest posts on the first of the month, so a quote expires then.

A sale also brings real estate excise tax, due to the county treasurer when the sale happens and normally the seller's cost. State rates are graduated, starting at 1.1% on the first $551,000 for sales on or after January 1, 2027 and topping out at 3.0% above $3,051,000. A local rate is added, and the Treasurer can give you the combined number.

After three years of delinquency, RCW 84.64.050 calls for certificates of delinquency and then foreclosure, though none can be filed on $100 or less. A resident owner within income limits can have interest and penalties waived once foreclosure starts (RCW 84.56.020).

Without a lender in the middle, a cash sale can close fast, with the title company paying the Treasurer from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

When are Snohomish County property taxes due?

Spring brings the first half or the full year, and fall the second half. Bills under $50 are due whole in April. Your next date is April 30, 2027.

How long do I have to appeal a Snohomish County property value?

Sixty calendar days from the date on your Notice of Value, or until July 1 of the assessment year, whichever is later. File with the Board of Equalization at 425-388-3407. Filing is free, but each parcel needs its own petition.

What is the interest on late Snohomish County property tax?

A home with four or fewer units accrues 9% a year with no penalty. Other property accrues 12% plus a 3% penalty after June 1 and 8% after December 1. Missing the April 30 half makes the full year delinquent.

Can I sell a Snohomish County house with back taxes?

Yes, if the unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid from the proceeds at closing. Call the Treasurer at 425-388-3366 for a payoff covering every year owed, and ask early.

Where do I pay Snohomish County property tax?

Online through the Treasurer's payment site, by card at 833-440-3332, by mail, or in the campus drop box in Everett. Send mail several days early, because checks can take a week or more to clear.

Mason County property tax offices

Property tax in Mason County passes through three Shelton offices. The Treasurer takes in the money, the Assessor determines value, and the Board of Equalization settles disputes. All use North Fifth Street addresses and share the county number 360-427-9670. Callers in Belfair can reach the Treasurer at 360-275-4467.

The Treasurer is on the second floor of Building 1, 411 N 5th Street, staffed 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, closed legal holidays. A drive-up drop box waits in the alley. Mail goes to the Mason County Treasurer's Office, PO Box 429, Shelton, WA 98584-0429. Dial extension 475 for the Treasurer and extension 491 for the Assessor. The county has an online tax search called TaxSifter, and card payments (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express) are accepted at the counter, online, or over the phone through Point N Pay, subject to a convenience fee under RCW 36.29.190.

Mason County market snapshot

Mason County has one incorporated city, Shelton, which is also the seat. Most residents live in unincorporated places such as Belfair, Allyn, Grapeview, Hoodsport, Skokomish and Union, and part of Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest lies inside the county.

  • Population in July 2025: 71,165, up 8.3% since April 2020.
  • Owners live in 82.3% of homes, so your competition is mostly other owners' listings.
  • A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $411,800.
  • Building permits in 2025: 204.

Due dates and late charges

The tax comes due in two payments, April 30 and October 31. A mailed payment is on time only if the postmark falls on or before the due date. Postal Service postmarks can lag, so send yours early.

The schedule is set in RCW 84.56.020. For a residence with up to four units, delinquent tax draws nine percent annual interest and no penalty. For all other property the interest is twelve percent, with a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1.

One side note for owners of several parcels: someone who paid a DNR fire patrol assessment on more than one Mason County parcel may be due a refund from the state Department of Natural Resources. Requests are due by December 31, 2026.

How do I appeal a Mason County assessment?

Appeals go to the Board of Equalization, 411 N 5th Street, Shelton, WA 98584-3466. Whichever is later sets your deadline: July 1 of the assessment year or the thirtieth day after the date on the Assessor's Notice of Change of Value. Mason County uses the 30-day rule in RCW 84.40.038. To get blank forms, ask the clerk at 360-427-9670 extension 268.

Deadlines can shift from year to year. In 2026 the Assessor dated its real property notices late, which pushed the appeal window into October. Do not rely on a calendar date from memory. The deadline for your case is printed on the notice.

The Board was created under chapter 84.48 RCW and works independently of the Assessor. It seats three members and two alternates on staggered three-year terms, and neither elected officials nor their employees may serve. It also hears appeals when the Assessor denies a senior citizen exemption. The county posts forms for real property, personal property, current use, senior exemption review, late filing exceptions and requests to reconvene the Board.

Relief programs and what you repay at sale

The Assessor administers five programs, two of which you must repay when you sell. Qualifying owners can choose among:

  • The senior citizen and disabled persons exemption, open at 61, on retirement for disability, or to a qualifying veteran.
  • A deferral for owners 60 or older, or retired for disability, where the state pays the tax and the deferred amount accrues 5% simple interest.
  • A limited-income deferral of the second-half installment, for owners with five years in the home, with applications due September 1.
  • A grant for the widow or widower of a veteran.
  • Current use classification for open space, farm and agricultural land, and designated forest land.

Both deferrals must be repaid once the home sells, the owner dies or the house is no longer the primary residence. That puts the deferred tax and interest on your closing statement, so request the balance from the Assessor before you list. The exemption has no repayment.

ESSB 6162 starts with the 2027 tax year. The Assessor describes it as raising income thresholds, giving a full exemption from the state school levy, and lowering the veteran disability rating needed from 80% to 40%. A $70,000 combined disposable income limit is listed for 2027, and renewals are required every three years. The statute is RCW 84.36.381.

Selling current use land

A parcel in the current use program is assessed at a reduced level because it is kept as open space, farm land or forest land. The application fee is $600 per parcel and is nonrefundable. Designated forest land needs a timber management plan with the first application, and again when the property is conveyed or sold.

That second filing lands on the seller's side of the table. If you hold forest land in Mason County, ask the Assessor what the buyer must file before the deed is signed. The Mason Conservation District offers technical and financial help to landowners, and the county page links the DNR's Find Your Forester tool.

If Mason County taxes are already behind

Call the Treasurer's Foreclosure Deputy at 360-427-9670 extension 485 before a parcel reaches a tax judgment sale. The county posts a foreclosure information sheet, a minimum bid sheet, public notices of judgment sales and a link to Bid4Assets, the online auction site.

The Treasurer points owners to three outside resources: the Washington Homeownership Resource Center at 1-877-894-4663, which gives free referrals, a nonprofit counseling agency called American Financial Solutions, and the Assessor's Office, which can say whether the senior or deferral programs fit a home with back taxes. Under RCW 84.56.020 the treasurer may arrange payment agreements for past due years, and an owner of limited income who occupies the home may ask for interest and penalties to be waived near the three-year mark while a foreclosure action is pending.

If you decide to sell, get the payoff figure first and let escrow pay it at closing. A cash buyer can often close fast enough to beat a judgment sale date.

Excise tax for a Mason County seller

Most of the time the seller bears Washington's real estate excise tax. When a seller leaves it unpaid, liability shifts to the buyer and a lien can follow. Payment is owed as of the sale date, and your deed, affidavit and check are presented to the county treasurer. Wait a month and 6% interest accrues from the sale date, the figure for both 2026 and 2027.

On sales starting January 1, 2027, state rates published by the Department of Revenue run 1.1% through $551,000, 1.28% through $1,551,000, 2.75% through $3,051,000 and 3.0% beyond that. A local rate is added. For the local figure and recording steps, call the Treasurer.

Whichever is later, July 1 or 30 days after the date on your Notice of Change of Value. Look at the notice itself, since mailing dates vary from year to year.

Yes. The deferred tax plus interest is owed at sale, at the owner's death, or when the home stops being the primary residence. Get the balance from the Assessor before listing.

The Treasurer's Foreclosure Deputy, at 360-427-9670 extension 485. The county's foreclosure page links to the minimum bid sheet and the Bid4Assets auction site.

Franklin County at a glance

Franklin County is where Pasco, the seat and biggest city, anchors the Tri-Cities alongside Kennewick and Richland, which are in neighboring Benton County. The 2020 count was 96,749 residents, up from 78,163 in 2010. The county held 29,740 housing units in 2020, with 3.3% vacant, and 68.3% of occupied homes were owned by their occupants. Four cities (Pasco, Connell, Mesa and Kahlotus) make up the incorporated area, so your tax code area and local excise rate depend on where the house sits.

Who handles property tax in Franklin County?

Property tax here passes through three desks. One sets values (Assessor), one rules on disputes (Board of Equalization), and one sends the bill and takes your money (Treasurer). The first two share the courthouse at 1016 N 4th Avenue, Pasco.

  • Assessor: Room A-104 in the basement. Call 509-545-3506. Open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Board of Equalization: Room A102. Phone 509-546-5855 weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., or email boeclerk@franklincountywa.gov.
  • Treasurer: collects both installments and runs the county's tax sales. Online account tools, a drive-up drop box and a paperless billing portal are offered.

Do not expect the Assessor to explain your rate or send a bill. The rate comes from voters, state limits and each taxing district's assessed value, and the Treasurer does the billing.

How often is a Franklin County house revalued?

A county appraiser must physically visit each parcel no less than every six years. In between, values are refreshed countywide every year using statistical analysis of sales. When comparable homes in an area keep selling above or below their assessed values, that area's roll is adjusted. A remodel, an addition or a subdivision earns a fresh value.

Real property is valued each January 1 for the following year's taxes (RCW 84.40.020). The mailing calendar runs like this: Change of Value Notices in the third quarter, tax statements in February. Since a summer notice looks back at last year's market, a fast change in prices may not be reflected yet.

Appraisers rely on sales comparison and cost for most homes, and the income approach mostly for business property. Pull your record before listing and check square footage, bedrooms and heating type against the house itself. A single wrong entry can move the value either way.

Due dates and penalties

Two installments are due, April 30 and October 31. Charges for lateness are added on the first of each month. Skip the first half and the entire year's tax goes delinquent, so interest runs on everything. Statements can fall on a weekend: October 31, 2026 was a Saturday, so ask the Treasurer how a Monday payment is treated in a year like that.

The rates come from RCW 84.56.020, and the Assessor posts the June 1 and December 1 dates on its important dates page.

How do you appeal a Franklin County assessment?

Your first move is to contact the Assessor, either by phone at 509-545-3506 or in Room A-104. Review how the value was figured, and ask the appraiser to line it up against recent sales nearby or to inspect the house. Still unhappy? The next step is a taxpayer petition to the Board of Equalization.

Your petition has to be mailed by July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the notice date, depending on which comes later. When that day is a weekend or holiday, you get the next business day. A postmark on or before the last day counts for mail. One form covers one parcel only.

Appraisals, maps, photos and letters must be submitted 21 days ahead of the hearing. The Board assumes the Assessor is correct, and under WAC 458-14-046 you must meet a standard of clear, cogent and convincing evidence to change that. If your proof is not ready, file a protective appeal before the cutoff to hold your place. Board sessions have run from October into January in recent cycles.

Tax relief programs

The Assessor lists several state programs. Each begins with a call to 509-545-3506.

  • Exemptions for senior citizens and disabled persons.
  • Exemptions for qualifying nonprofit property.
  • A destroyed property claim, which adjusts the value of damaged buildings.
  • A historical restoration exemption for significant property under restoration.
  • Open space classification for agricultural land, timberland and nature preserves.

Nonprofit exemption applications must reach the Department of Revenue by March 31. Farm open space applications are treated as approved on May 1 unless the Assessor says otherwise.

Paying your Franklin County taxes

Phone payments ended on January 1, 2024. Pay through the online portal, mail a check, or walk in. A drive-up drop box sits under the blue banner across from the security building.

Sign up for email reminders each April and October on the paperless tax bill page, and staff will help you set up the account. The office also offers several payment plan options, so call before an account slips far behind. To change an address, use the Assessor's page after confirming the address with the postal service.

If a parcel goes to tax sale, the county advertises it at least three weeks ahead in the Franklin County Graphic and the Tri-City Herald. State law lets the treasurer foreclose on parcels with unpaid taxes, so an old balance is worth clearing early.

What you owe when you sell

When a Washington house sells, real estate excise tax follows, normally at the seller's expense. Payment goes to the treasurer of the county that holds the property and is owed as of the sale date, even if the deed is recorded later. After a month, interest and penalties begin.

State rates come from a sliding scale at the Department of Revenue, with price breaks at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000 starting January 1, 2027. Your town adds its own local rate. The Treasurer or your closing agent can quote the combined figure for Pasco or the town where you live.

If property tax is still owed, request a payoff figure from the Treasurer and pay it out of closing proceeds so the buyer gets clean title. Buyers who pay cash skip a lender's appraisal and underwriting, which removes steps that often slow a closing. For a quick sale, line up the payoff number, the excise tax and the deed paperwork before you accept an offer.

When are Franklin County property taxes due?

Installments fall on April 30 and October 31. Miss the first and the full year is delinquent, with interest or penalties on the entire amount.

How do I appeal my Franklin County property value?

Talk to the Assessor at 509-545-3506 first. If that does not resolve it, petition the Board of Equalization by the later of July 1 or 30 days after the notice. The clerk's number is 509-546-5855.

Can I pay Franklin County property tax by phone?

No. The Treasurer stopped taking phone payments on January 1, 2024. Use the online portal, mail, the counter or the drive-up drop box.

How often does Franklin County inspect homes?

At least once every six years in person. Values are also updated every year across the county through analysis of sales.

Who pays excise tax when you sell in Franklin County?

Normally the seller. The tax goes to the county treasurer and is owed on the sale date, combining a price-based state rate with a local rate.

  • Treasurer: 35 C Street NW, Room 204, Ephrata, mailing address P.O. Box 37. Phone 509-754-2010. Open weekdays but closed from noon to 1 p.m.
  • Board of Equalization: handles valuation appeals. For help locating comparable sales, ring the Assessor's Office at 509-754-2011 ext. 2683.

The Treasurer's website has a searchable tax statement for 2025 and 2026 and a parcel lookup, so you can get a payoff picture without a trip to Ephrata. Mailing address changes and quit claim forms also go through that office.

How the Assessor values your house

Valuation happens as of January 1, and all properties get new values every year. An old appeal does not roll forward, so protecting your rights means filing a new petition each year.

Owners of older homes and farmland should note two programs. State law sets April 1 as the deadline for senior and disabled tax deferral applications. Exemption claims for seniors and disabled owners can go in at any time of year and apply to the next year's taxes. Open space (current use) filings count as approved on May 1 unless the Assessor tells you otherwise, and you can apply for the next year's valuation anytime from January 1 through December 31.

Senior exemption income limits were updated for the 2027 tax year. Phone the Assessor for today's limit before you count on any figure.

Important Grant County tax dates

The bill is split in half, due April 30 and October 31, and a post office postmark counts as paid on time. Late payments pick up interest, and some property types pick up penalties too.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for real property
April 1Senior and disabled deferral applications due
April 30First half of taxes due
June 13% penalty on delinquent tax, where state law applies it
July 1Last day to petition the Board of Equalization, or 30 days after the notice if later
October 31Second half due (a Saturday in 2026)
December 1Additional 8% penalty on delinquent tax, where state law applies it

Houses and other residential property of four units or fewer pay interest alone, at 9% a year for taxes levied in 2023 and later. Everything else pays 12% a year and both penalties. The rules sit in RCW 84.56.020, and the Assessor posts the calendar on its important dates page.

How do you appeal a Grant County assessment?

Talk to the Assessor before anything else. A conversation may fix a record error, and if not, you take the dispute to the Board of Equalization. The petition counts as timely when it lands by July 1 of the assessment year, or within 30 calendar days of the notice date if that gives you more time. Mailed petitions need a postmark inside the window. Nothing is charged to file, and one parcel means one petition.

  • Fill in the parcel number, your contact details, what the property is, the Assessor's number, what you think it is worth and why. Sign, date and attach the notice.
  • Attach comparable sales, repair bids, an appraisal or photos. Sales near January 1 carry the most weight.
  • Supporting evidence added later must be at the Board 21 business days before the hearing.

Expect the Board to start from the assumption that the Assessor got it right. Overcoming that takes clear, cogent and convincing evidence, and your hardship or the size of the bill will not be weighed. You will get at least 30 business days' warning of the hearing date. The losing side may go on to the state Board of Tax Appeals, filing within 30 days.

Paying, and what to do if you are behind

Options are mail, the counter, or Point & Pay online. Online fees are 2.7% for credit cards, 0.95% for debit and $1.30 for an eCheck, and a returned payment carries a $30 fee. Online payments take three to five business days to appear.

The Treasurer posts a delinquent tax payment plan application, plus an interest waiver application for a principal residence heading into foreclosure. The office also holds an annual tax foreclosure sale on the Public Surplus website; the 2026 sale ran November 9 and 10. Owners far behind should phone the Treasurer at 509-754-2010 long before the next sale. Washington law also gives an owner with limited income who lives in the house a chance to ask for interest and penalties to be waived as the third anniversary of delinquency approaches.

Closing on a Grant County sale

At closing, the deed and an excise tax affidavit both go to the Treasurer of the county where the home is. State forms and the exemption code list are linked from the Treasurer's page, plus a lack of probate affidavit for deeds where nobody opened probate.

Sellers normally owe the excise tax on the date of sale. Price sets the state rate and the city adds a local one, so ask the Treasurer for the total for your location. Blank deed and quit claim forms are posted there as well, and if yours needs drafting, a title company or attorney can do it.

A workable order: pull a tax statement and payoff figure, confirm the excise rate, gather the deed and affidavit, and have the title company clear any balance out of proceeds. If the buyer pays cash, no lender signs off, one less thing that can delay closing. Ask the title company early whether it needs a recent statement, since the Treasurer's online tools cover 2025 and 2026.

Frequently asked questions

When are Grant County property taxes due?

One half is owed by April 30 and the rest by October 31. A postmark from the post office works, and late balances pick up interest.

How long do I have to appeal my Grant County assessment?

You have until July 1 of the assessment year, or until 30 calendar days after the value change notice if that date is later. Mailed petitions need a postmark by then, and filing is free.

Does Grant County revalue homes every year?

Yes, every year, and last year's appeal does not carry forward. File a new petition annually.

How much does it cost to pay Grant County taxes online?

Expect 2.7% on credit cards, 0.95% on debit and $1.30 on an eCheck. A check by mail or at the counter has no vendor fee.

Does Grant County hold a tax foreclosure sale?

Yes, annually, on the Public Surplus website. The 2026 edition ran November 9 and 10. Phone 509-754-2010 to learn the next date.

Who to call about Clark County property tax

Clark County splits the job in two. The Treasurer sends bills and takes payments; the Assessor decides what your property is worth on paper. You will find both at the Public Service Center, 1300 Franklin Street, Vancouver. If you want to talk in person, go to the second-floor Joint Lobby, which is open Monday through Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

  • Treasurer: 564-397-2252 or treasoff@clark.wa.gov. Phone and email hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Assessor: 564-397-2391. Appraisers cover every taxable real and personal property, walking through roughly one-sixth of the county's parcels each year.
  • Questions about senior or disability relief: taxreduction@clark.wa.gov.

About 50 public service providers share in the revenue, among them schools, fire districts, ports, cemetery districts and cities. Whatever levy rates apply to the districts over your lot get added together on your statement.

Clark County market snapshot

Clark County faces Portland across the Columbia River, and Vancouver is its biggest city. Population reached about 532,119 in July 2025, compared with 503,311 in 2020. Owner-occupants live in 66.4 percent of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $522,900. Builders pulled 3,250 permits in 2025, so buyers in your area often have new construction to compare against your house.

Due dates and late payment charges

Statements split the year into two halves. Half one is due April 30 and half two October 31, as set by RCW 84.56.020. In 2026 the second date fell on a Saturday, so the Treasurer moved the deadline to Monday, November 2. Expect the same shift whenever a due date lands on a weekend.

  • Statements usually become available by March 15 for the first half and September 15 for the second.
  • A mailed check is timely only when the USPS postmark shows the due date or earlier. Collection boxes can miss that day's postmark, so the Treasurer recommends handing the envelope to a postal clerk, or paying by e-check.
  • You can send less than the full amount. Still, the minimum billed has to arrive by each deadline, otherwise interest and penalties build on whatever stays unpaid.
  • Late residential parcels with up to four units accrue 0.75 percent per month and no penalty. Any other parcel accrues 1 percent per month, and takes a 3 percent penalty on June 1 and an 8 percent penalty on December 1.
  • You cannot prepay a future year, with a narrow carve-out when selling personal property or a mobile home.

Paying the Treasurer

An e-check costs nothing, which makes it the least expensive choice. On the online payment site, look up your parcel by last name or account number, check what you owe, and enroll in paperless billing if you like.

  • By phone, call Point & Pay at 1-833-440-8685 and use an e-check, debit card or credit card. A debit payment adds a flat $3.95. A credit payment adds 2.39 percent.
  • By mail, write a check or money order to Clark County Treasurer. Put the account number and tax year on the memo line. Including the stub helps but is optional.
  • After a certificate of delinquency is filed in a foreclosure, only the owner or a person with a recorded interest in the parcel may pay.

Selling with property tax due

A lien for the year's property tax attaches on January 1. Where your purchase contract is silent, RCW 84.60.020 has you covering the days before closing and the buyer the days after. Ask the closing agent to pull the Treasurer's present balance, so the split rests on actual figures and not on last year's statement.

The state's real estate excise tax is charged on the sale. The county treasurer where the property sits collects it, and sellers usually bear it. Put it in your net proceeds estimate next to any property tax still owed.

Homeowners with a senior or disability exemption should know what happens to it. The Assessor's FAQ explains that it can follow you to a new primary residence if you still qualify, but you reapply for that home and send income documents again. Only one primary residence can hold the exemption.

Is your Clark County valuation too high?

Appeal the assessed value within 60 days of the date printed on your Notice of Value, if you think it is above market value. Hearing that your bill went up is not a reason on its own, because the Assessor says growth in the tax amount is not appealable.

Bills rise for two common reasons. Levies that voters approved sit outside the 1 percent limit. Also, a house that gains value faster than average carries a bigger slice of each district's levy. That 1 percent limit controls what a district collects overall, adjusted for new construction, and says nothing about one household's bill.

Before you phone, open the county's Property Information Center. It lists your assessed value, the building characteristics on file, and how the bill divides among school, city and other districts. Compare those details with the house you actually own. State law (RCW 84.40.038) also lets the board of equalization excuse a late filing when there is good cause.

2027 changes to the senior exemption

Tax year 2027 brings much higher income limits. Senate Bill 6162 sets each tier at 80 percent of county median household income for tax years 2027 to 2029. Approved applicants will also be exempt from all state school levies, a veteran needs only a 40 percent disability rating, and a $7,500 standard deduction applies for each applicant and spouse.

Income tierLimit, tax years 2024 to 2026Limit, tax years 2027 to 2029
Threshold 1$44,000$64,000
Threshold 2$53,000$74,000
Threshold 3$62,000$85,000
Senior deferral limit$65,548$94,579

Who can apply: people who turn 61 by December 31 of the assessment year, people unable to work because of a disability, and anyone who is a qualifying disabled veteran. You must own the house and occupy it six months or more each year. Current participants are adjusted without doing anything. New applications open in February 2027 online, by mail or at an appointment. A benefit may include a freeze on assessed value for that year, and the difference in tax is neither repaid nor recorded as a lien.

When taxes are behind

Send what you can. The Treasurer applies partial payments to the oldest balance first. An owner with limited income who lives in the home and faces foreclosure or distraint may qualify for a one-time waiver of interest and penalties. To speak with a tax specialist, write to taxrequests@clark.wa.gov.

Real property that is three or more years delinquent can be foreclosed under chapter 84.64 RCW. The Washington Homeownership Resource Center, 877-894-4663, helps with foreclosure prevention, housing counseling and legal questions.

Planning a sale while taxes are owed? Request a payoff balance from the Treasurer before choosing a closing date, then have the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds. A cash buyer skips lender underwriting and appraisal, which shortens the timeline, though the lien must still be cleared at closing.

Frequently asked questions

When are Clark County property taxes due?

April 30 covers the first half and October 31 the second. In 2026 the second date landed on a weekend, so the Treasurer moved it to Monday, November 2. Mail needs a USPS postmark on or before the deadline.

What does late payment cost in Clark County?

Residential parcels of four units or fewer owe 0.75 percent interest each month and no penalties. Everything else owes 1 percent monthly, with a 3 percent penalty added June 1 and an 8 percent penalty added December 1.

Can I pay Clark County property tax by phone?

Yes, through Point and Pay at 1-833-440-8685, using an e-check, debit card or credit card. Debit adds $3.95, credit adds 2.39 percent, and e-check is free. The main office line does not take payments.

How long do I have to appeal my Clark County value?

Sixty days from the date on your Notice of Value. Call the Assessor at 564-397-2391 with questions. Only the assessed value can be appealed, not a bill increase that comes from voted levies or district budgets.

What will the senior exemption income limit be in Clark County in 2027?

The highest tier moves to $85,000 for tax years 2027 to 2029, and the lower tiers to $74,000 and $64,000. You qualify if you are 61 or older, cannot work because of a disability, or are a qualifying disabled veteran, and you own and live in the home.

Whatcom County in brief

Whatcom County fills the northwest corner of Washington, with British Columbia to the north and the Strait of Georgia to the west. It spans 2,503 square miles and had 226,847 residents in the 2020 census. Bellingham is both the county seat and the largest city here. Blaine, Everson, Ferndale, Lynden, Nooksack and Sumas are the other incorporated cities, and the county also holds Lummi and Nooksack tribal lands, Birch Bay, Point Roberts, Sudden Valley and Geneva.

Two neighbors a few miles apart can pay different tax rates, because every parcel belongs to its own mix of city, school, fire and other districts.

Which Whatcom County offices handle property tax?

Three offices matter to an owner, and each has its own job.

  • Assessor. Fixes every parcel's value on January 1 of the assessment year, using July 31 for new construction. Phone 360-778-5050. The same office runs the senior and disability exemption.
  • Treasurer. Bills and collects real and personal property tax, takes the real estate excise tax on sales, and runs tax foreclosure. The counter is on the courthouse first floor at 311 Grand Avenue, Suite 104, Bellingham, open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon. Phone 360-778-5160. Drop boxes are near the north rotunda entrance, outside the south entrance and outside the Treasurer's lobby.
  • Board of Equalization. Handles disputes over value. Three regular members and four alternates sit on it, all appointed by the County Council.

The Treasurer's website offers online payment, tax lookup and foreclosure auction notices.

Due dates and mailing

The two halves fall on April 30 and October 31. Statements are mailed in February, and RCW 84.56.020 calls for a statement by March 15 when the budget and levy steps finish on time. A due date on a weekend counts as the following business day. Mailed checks are judged by the post office postmark, never a postage machine date, so on the due date ask the counter clerk to hand-cancel your envelope.

Tax payments are mailed to Whatcom County Treasurer, PO Box 34873, Seattle, WA 98124-1873. Use that box for tax only. Paying in halves is open to anyone whose total is $50 or more. A late first half is still accepted until October 31, with interest and any penalty figured on the whole year.

Late charges run on a fixed schedule:

  • A home of up to four units, manufactured homes too, is charged 9 percent interest a year and never a penalty.
  • Other property carries 12 percent interest, a 3 percent penalty on taxes still delinquent June 1 and another 8 percent on December 1.
  • Any delinquent year can be paid in full, with interest and penalty, without first paying the current year.
  • Foreclosure on real property starts when tax is three years delinquent, and the Treasurer holds a tax foreclosure auction each November.

Owners who live in the home and meet the income test can have leftover interest and penalties waived, just short of the three-year mark, once foreclosure is filed. The waiver is available one time per property.

Whatcom County tax rates

No single rate covers the county. The Assessor's 2026 report sets a levy rate per $1,000 of assessed value for each taxing district, and your bill adds the districts over your parcel. To estimate a bill, divide assessed value by 1,000 and multiply by the combined rate. Here is a sample of 2026 rates:

Taxing district2026 levy rate per $1,000

Fire districts, ports and other districts add more where they serve a parcel. Countywide assessed value rose about 1.2 percent for 2026, and most of the increase in bills came from voter-approved measures instead of value growth. Staff physically inspect one-sixth of the county every year. Area 5, which included mid-Bellingham, Geneva and Sudden Valley, was inspected in 2026, and area 6 is next in 2027.

How do I appeal a Whatcom County assessment?

Fill out the state form and send it to the county's equalization board. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due July 1 of the assessment year, or 30 days after the notice mailing, or up to 60 days where the county legislative authority adopted a longer period. The later date wins. Your Change of Value notice states the deadline that applies, so read it when it arrives.

The Board values property at 100 percent of market value and may lower, raise or keep your number. A late petition can be accepted for good cause such as serious illness, a natural disaster or postal delay. Appeals of a Board decision go to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals. Before you file, talk with an appraiser at the Assessor's office, who can explain how your number was reached.

Tax relief for Whatcom County homeowners

Two programs matter most to owners under financial strain.

  • Senior and disability exemption. For 2026 taxes, the earlier qualifications still apply. A 2026 law change raises the income limit to $72,000 beginning with 2026 income, which affects 2027 taxes. It adds a standard deduction of $7,500 per person or $15,000 per couple, lowers the qualifying disability rating from 80 to 40 percent, and exempts participants from the state school levy in full. Three income levels, $54,000, $63,000 and $72,000, set how much assessed value is exempt from regular levies. Apply through the Assessor in person or online.
  • Destroyed property. After the December 2025 flooding, the Assessor lowered values on affected parcels in Sumas, Nooksack, Everson and Ferndale for the 2025/26 year. Values return to market for 2027 taxes. The Assessor's destroyed property coordinator handles claims for parcels still damaged.

Washington also runs a deferral program under chapter 84.38 RCW, and every tax statement must mention it. Ask the Assessor's office whether you qualify.

Taxes when you sell a Whatcom County house

Before the County Auditor records a deed, the Treasurer must receive a real estate excise tax affidavit and the payment, for every kind of transfer. An incomplete affidavit is rejected, and the staff cannot provide legal advice on filling it out. Interest and penalty start 30 days after the sale date. Have your escrow or title officer request a payoff from the Treasurer for any delinquent years and for the current half before closing day.

A gift transfer needs a supplemental statement signed by both parties, and a minimum filing fee applies when no tax is due. Mobile homes have extra steps: a mobile home that will be moved needs a tax certificate from the Assessor and an orange decal from the Treasurer. State rates and exemptions are on the Washington Department of Revenue real estate excise tax page and the county's excise tax page.

Papers to gather before closing

Pull these items together a few weeks ahead so escrow has what it needs.

  • Your parcel number and the latest statement, so the title officer can order the payoff.
  • Proof of which half you have paid, with receipts if you paid by mail.
  • The names of both parties for the excise tax affidavit, and the exemption reason if the sale is a gift or another exempt transfer.
  • Any exemption or deferral paperwork, so the Assessor can tell you what ends at sale.

Cash buyers usually close faster because there is no lender underwriting, but the Treasurer's payoff and the excise tax filing are the same either way.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Whatcom County deadlines?

The first half is owed April 30 and the second October 31. A weekend due date slides forward, and the postmark from the post office, not the sender, sets the date on a mailed check.

What happens if I do not pay Whatcom County property tax?

Interest starts after the due date, at 9 percent a year on a home of four or fewer units. Foreclosure begins once taxes are three years delinquent, with an auction each November. Income-qualified owners living in the home can ask about a waiver of interest and penalties.

How do I check what I owe in Whatcom County?

Use the Treasurer's online tax lookup or call 360-778-5160. Tax records are public. If you are selling, ask for the payoff for each delinquent year as well as the current year.

Can I appeal my Whatcom County property value?

Yes. The board decides them. Look at your Change of Value notice. The cutoff is July 1 or the end of the notice period, 30 days or up to 60 if the county chose that, whichever lands later. The Assessor at 360-778-5050 can review the value with you first.

Who is responsible for excise tax on a Whatcom sale?

The seller pays. The Treasurer collects it with an affidavit before the deed is recorded, and interest and penalty start 30 days after the sale date. Escrow normally takes it from the seller's proceeds.

Older bills, from before 2023, accrue at 1% per month. The county cannot waive charges if it mailed the statement to an address you or your agent, for instance a closing agent, provided. One hardship waiver exists, for a personal residence where a spouse's, parent's or stepparent's death caused the missed payment, and it requires telling the treasurer and paying within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025).

To preserve a right to sue for a refund, a payment under protest must be written down and sent along with the payment (RCW 84.68.020). A returned bank item adds a $30 fee.

How your house is valued

Each parcel is revalued every year as of January 1, with a physical visit at least every six years. New construction is appraised annually and owners are notified of changes. The target is full market value, worked out from comparable sales, depreciated replacement cost or income methods.

Your Official Assessment Notice shows up in June, yet levy rates are not set until mid-January of the next year, so the notice cannot tell you the final tax. Bills are not capped at a 1% increase either. That cap touches some taxing district budgets, and special levies, banked capacity and annexations muddy it. In a flat or cooling market, assessments flatten too, since they follow sales data.

How to appeal your assessment

Send a petition to the County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year, or 30 days after the Change of Value Notice went out if that is later. Mail it with a postmark by midnight of the deadline or hand-deliver it for a date stamp. It is free, and a letter or phone call cannot replace the form.

  • State specific reasons the value is wrong and include the parcel number, the Assessor's figure and your own estimate. The board will not weigh your tax amount, other properties' values, the size of the jump or hardship.
  • Anything extra must reach the board a week or so beforehand, specifically seven business days.
  • You can settle with the Assessor through a stipulation of value, or drop the appeal by withdrawal.
  • Within 30 calendar days of the decision you can go to the State Board of Tax Appeals, or you can pay under protest and sue for a refund under chapter 84.68 RCW.

The Assessor starts out presumed correct, and only clear, cogent and convincing evidence overcomes that (RCW 84.40.0301). Keep paying while the case is open. Buyers get an exception: the board can meet again after the deadline for a home bought between July 1 and December 31 of the assessment year at under 90% of assessed value.

Senior and disability exemption

A senior exemption exists for owner-occupants 62 or older whose household income is under $50,000. Apply with the form on the Assessor's site or call 509-477-3698. New income thresholds start in 2027 under Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, and since the numbers are changing, ask the Assessor for current limits.

People retired because of a disability are covered too. After processing, the Treasurer sends you or your mortgage company a corrected statement.

Paying off a mortgage mid-year? Tell the Treasurer so billing details change and a duplicate bill reaches you.

Selling with back taxes

Ask the Treasurer for a written payoff covering every unpaid year ahead of closing, and have the closing agent pay it from the sale money. Interest builds monthly, so the number keeps moving.

Mail matters here. If the Treasurer sends a bill to the address your closing agent gave and it goes unpaid, the county cannot waive the interest, so confirm the agent has the correct parcel number and a forwarding address that works.

The seller normally owes real estate excise tax, payable to the county treasurer when the sale occurs. State rates rise with price. In the schedule for sales from January 1, 2027, one tier is 1.28% between $551,000 and $1,551,000. A local rate sits on top, and the Treasurer can quote the total.

Left unpaid three years from delinquency, a parcel faces certificates of delinquency and foreclosure under RCW 84.64.050. Any payment on past-due tax must first cover the oldest delinquent year with interest and penalties (RCW 84.56.020). Cash sales skip the lender, and the title company can settle with the Treasurer from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

When are Spokane County property taxes due?

Each half has its own date, April 30 and October 31, and a bill under $50 is due entirely in April. The next one for you is April 30, 2027, or the next business day if a holiday intervenes.

What if I never received my Spokane County tax statement?

Call the Treasurer at 509-477-4713, or check the SCOUT site, if nothing has come by March 31. A bill that never arrives does not cancel interest or penalty, because paying remains your responsibility.

How long do I have to appeal my Spokane County assessment?

The later of July 1 of the assessment year and 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed. The petition is free, and your payments should continue during the appeal.

What interest does Spokane County charge on late tax?

Homes of four or fewer units pay 0.75% a month and no penalty. Other property pays 1% a month plus 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1. Interest is figured on the full year, beginning May 1 for the first half.

Can I sell a Spokane County house that owes back taxes?

Yes, when the unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid at closing. Get a payoff from the Treasurer at 509-477-4713, and sell or pay before three years of delinquency lets the county begin foreclosure.

Thurston County property tax offices

Property tax work is split among three offices in the Atrium building, 3000 Pacific Ave SE, Olympia. The Treasurer sends statements and takes payment. The Assessor decides values and runs exemptions. Value appeals go before the Board of Equalization.

  • Treasurer: 360-786-5550, trsr@co.thurston.wa.us, weekday hours run 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m.

  • Board of Equalization: 360-786-5135. Outside appeal season, visits are by appointment only.

Notices for 2026 were mailed February 9, 2026, covering a total assessed value of $652,290,192 across all taxing districts.

Thurston County market basics

Thurston County lies at the south end of Puget Sound along I-5. Olympia, the state capital, is the county seat. Lacey, Tumwater, Yelm and Bucoda are the other incorporated places, and Lacey, with an estimated population above 60,000, is now larger than Olympia. More than 145,000 people live outside any city, mostly between Olympia and Lacey. State government jobs have anchored the local housing market for decades.

  • Population: 304,261 in July 2025, on 722.5 square miles of land.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 67.7 percent.

Thurston County due dates

A first-half payment is late after April 30, and a second-half payment is late after October 31. If a deadline lands on a Saturday or Sunday, it slides to the following Monday. Choose a payment route from the table below.

One quirk: a half payment on real property is good only until October 30. After that date the Treasurer wants the entire year's balance. Hardship extensions are not allowed under the law.
