What happens when Thurston County taxes are late?

Interest builds on the whole year's tax from the delinquency date, and real property can be sold for taxes once it is three full years behind. RCW 84.56.020 sets residential interest at 9 percent a year for properties of four units or fewer. Other property types also take a 3 percent penalty on June 1 and an 8 percent penalty on December 1. Call 360-786-5550 for the exact amount on your parcel.

  • A late payment must include the late charges or the Treasurer sends it back.
  • Foreclosure on real property begins each June and ends with a sale in the second week of January.
  • A signed payment plan is possible for delinquent prior years. Tax for the current year has to be paid whole.
  • Delinquent tax is never reported to credit agencies, but an owner's name goes into a legal notice in a local newspaper.
  • If the sale brings in more than the tax and costs, the owner receives the surplus.

Special assessments on the bill are enforceable liens too. Stormwater, state forest fire protection, noxious weed control, conservation district, drainage district, lake management and septic program charges all fall in that group, and the Treasurer will not take the tax without them.

How to appeal a Thurston County assessment

Send the Board of Equalization a signed petition by July 1, or within 60 days after the Assessor mails your value notice if that date is later. Each parcel needs its own petition, on the county form with an original signature, along with a copy of the front page of the value notice. Email, fax and online filing are not accepted. Mail, courier and hand delivery work, and a mailed petition has to be postmarked by the deadline.

The board looks at market value and nothing else. It cannot weigh the amount of tax, other properties' assessments, the percentage increase or personal hardship. Since the Assessor's number starts out presumed right, the owner has to bring clear, cogent and convincing proof such as comparable sales, repair bids and photos.

Expect a wait, because hearings can take 12 to 18 months to be scheduled. Late-filing exceptions are narrow and must be requested by April 30 of the following year. If the board rules against you, the State Board of Tax Appeals will hear a further appeal filed within 30 days. File again every year you disagree, since each petition stands alone.

Property tax relief

The senior and disability exemption is the largest program, run by the Assessor. You qualify if you are 61 or older, disabled and unable to work, or rated 80 percent or higher for a service-connected disability (40 percent beginning in 2027). You must also own and live in the home, with combined disposable income of $59,000 or less, rising to $83,000 beginning in 2027.

Qualifying owners are exempt from voted taxes, which make up about 40 percent of a typical Thurston County bill, and the taxable value of the home is frozen. While an application is pending you still owe what is billed on the due date, and a refund follows if the Assessor approves.

Other programs to ask about:

  • Senior and limited-income deferral, where the state pays the second half and places a lien. The limited-income version has a $57,000 income cap and needs five years of ownership.
  • Relief for destroyed property, which must be claimed within three years of the loss.
  • A three-year residential remodeling exemption, which has to be filed before work begins.
  • Current use classification for farm, timber and open space land.

Property tax at a Thurston County closing

The tax stays with the land rather than the seller, and the contract between you and the buyer decides how the year is divided. The state default in RCW 84.60.020 prorates by the part of the calendar year before and after the sale date, with the lien attaching on January 1.

Statements go out only once a year, in February, to the owner on record as of December 31. After a sale the new owner may never receive a bill, so tell the escrow officer which half is still open and let the title company confirm with the Treasurer. The owner name on the tax roll changes when the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit is filed with the county.

A seller's checklist for Thurston County

These steps help you reach closing without a tax surprise.

  • Call the Treasurer at 360-786-5550 and ask whether the first and second halves are both paid and whether any older year is open.
  • Look at the bill for special assessments such as stormwater or septic charges, since those travel with the parcel.
  • If you hold an exemption or a deferral, call the Assessor at 360-867-2200 to learn what happens when you sell.
  • If a signed payment plan covers a prior year, tell escrow so the balance can be paid at closing.
  • Pass the buyer's contact details to the title company, because the buyer may not get a statement until the following February.

Cash buyers skip lender conditions, so the tax payoff is often one of the few items left to sort out in the final week.

Frequently asked questions

What is the fall deadline in Thurston County?

October 31. Weekend deadlines roll to Monday. Call the Treasurer at 360-786-5550 for your balance and any late charges.

Can I get an extension on Thurston County property tax?

No. The law allows no extensions for hardship. A payment plan is available for delinquent prior years, and the senior and disability exemption or deferral may reduce or postpone tax if you qualify.

When can I appeal my Thurston County assessed value?

Once a year. The cutoff is July 1, or 60 days after the value notice was mailed if that falls later. Each petition stands alone, so file every year you disagree.

How long before Thurston County forecloses on unpaid property tax?

Real property becomes subject to sale when taxes are three full years delinquent. Foreclosure begins in June and the sale is held in the second week of January.

Mid-year sale in Thurston County: who pays the tax?

The purchase contract can say anything it likes. If it is silent, the seller is responsible for the months before closing and the buyer for the months after, and escrow settles the open half with the Treasurer.

Douglas County in brief

Douglas County hugs the Columbia River in north-central Washington. The seat is Waterville, though East Wenatchee has the most people, and the county is counted in the Wenatchee metro area. Three cities (Bridgeport, East Wenatchee and Rock Island) and several towns share the land. The city or town your parcel falls in matters at sale time, because the local excise tax rate depends on location.

The 2020 count was 42,938 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 46,473. Of 17,318 housing units in 2020, 11.0% were vacant, and owners lived in 70.7% of the occupied ones.

Offices that handle Douglas County property tax

Four separate offices touch your tax: Assessor, Treasurer, Auditor and Board of Equalization. Most sit on South Rainier Street in Waterville.

  • Assessor: 213 S Rainier Street, mailing address P.O. Box 387, Waterville. Phone 509-745-8521. The counter is staffed weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Treasurer: in the same building, mailing address P.O. Box 609. Call 509-745-8525. Excise tax on sales and tax foreclosures also run through this desk.
  • Auditor: records deeds. Call 509-745-8527.
  • Board of Equalization: 203 S Rainier, Waterville, P.O. Box 747. Call 509-745-8537.

The Treasurer also bills under contract for five irrigation districts, so your statement may include irrigation charges on top of the property tax.

How the Assessor values a house

Every parcel is valued at 100% of market value, as Washington law requires, and Douglas County redoes every value each year. When a number looks wrong, ring 509-745-8521 first and walk the appraiser through what you see. That route can fix a simple record error without a hearing.

Relief programs mostly turn on age and income. The senior exemption may fit residents 61 or older, people who retired because of disability, and a veteran with a qualifying disability, with household income deciding. The Assessor's page links a screening tool, but staff make the final call. Farmland may qualify for open space treatment, and the office also has forms for current use, combining parcels, destroyed property and address changes.

Property tax funds cities, the county, fire protection, law enforcement, libraries, parks, roads and schools. Which of these your parcel pays depends on where it sits.

Due dates, fees and late charges

Your bill comes due in two installments, April 30 and October 31. In 2026 October 31 landed on a Saturday, and a Monday payment dated November 2 raised a question, so check with the Treasurer on how a weekend deadline is treated if you are cutting it close. If you miss the first installment, the full year's tax becomes delinquent under RCW 84.56.020, with interest figured monthly.

To pay, phone Point and Pay at 866-898-2916 or use the TaxSifter parcel search online. A payment must be processed before 11:59 p.m. Pacific time to count for that day, yet it is not posted in real time, so budget two to three business days. Vendor fees: a flat $2.30 for eCheck, 2.7% for credit cards and 0.95% for debit. The Personal Teller live-agent service adds $5.

Residential property with four units or fewer owes 9% a year and no penalties. Other property owes 12% a year plus penalties of 3% and then 8%.

How to appeal your assessment

The county commissioners make up the Board of Equalization. They bring in an independent hearing examiner to conduct hearings and recommend outcomes, and the board and its clerk stay separate from the Assessor.

A finished petition must be in by July 1 of the assessment year. If your Change of Value Notice was mailed later, you instead get 30 days from the mailing date. Whichever date is later controls, and the filing must be filed or postmarked by it.

  • Email: BOE@CO.DOUGLAS.WA.US, received by 5 p.m.
  • Mail: Douglas County Board of Equalization, P.O. Box 747, Waterville, WA 98858.
  • In person: Public Service Building, 140 19th Street NW, East Wenatchee.

Do not hold back payment while an appeal is pending. If the value is lowered, the county credits your account with the difference. The county also has a waiver of late filing request form, and a late petition can sometimes be excused for good cause.

Excise tax when you sell

Nearly every sale in Washington carries real estate excise tax, and WAC 458-61A-301 puts it on the seller. The Treasurer takes it in as the state's agent. Bring the sale in within 30 days of the sale date or interest and penalties start.

The order of stops matters: Treasurer with the excise tax affidavit and deed, then the Auditor for recording. Count on 10 to 20 minutes per document, a first come first served line, and a 4 p.m. cutoff for recording. Title companies and attorneys can skip the trip and file through Simplifile. Courthouse staff cannot write or review a deed, and mobile or manufactured home sales have special requirements, so call 509-745-8525 before you go.

The state portion is added to the local rate and graduates with price. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 follow the Department of Revenue schedule: 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000 and 3% above.

What to bring to the courthouse: the signed deed, the completed excise tax affidavit, and the parcel number. Mobile or manufactured home sales need extra paperwork, so ask first.

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid taxes can end in foreclosure, since the Treasurer is legally required to seize and sell delinquent property. Short of that, the state lets the Treasurer set up payment agreements and take partial payments, oldest year first. A low-income owner who lives in the house may request a waiver of interest and penalties once the parcel is facing foreclosure, beginning 60 days ahead of the third anniversary of delinquency.

Phone 509-745-8525 for a payoff figure before you pick a closing date. Because interest accrues monthly, last month's number may fall short. Give the final amount to your title company, which will pay the lien from your proceeds at closing. A cash buyer needs no lender approval, which can help when a payoff deadline is near.

A simple order of steps: get the payoff figure, confirm the local excise rate for your city, gather the deed and affidavit, and give the Treasurer the sale within the 30-day window. Doing the property tax payoff and the excise filing together keeps the county's records clean for the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

When are Douglas County property taxes due?

April 30 and October 31. If the first installment is missed, the whole year's tax is delinquent.

Where do I file a Douglas County appeal?

Email BOE@CO.DOUGLAS.WA.US by 5 p.m., mail it to P.O. Box 747, Waterville, or bring it to the Public Service Building at 140 19th Street NW in East Wenatchee. File by July 1, or within 30 days of your notice if that is later.

How much does it cost to pay Douglas County taxes by card?

The vendor charges 2.7% on credit and 0.95% on debit. An eCheck is a flat $2.30.

What is the excise tax rate in East Wenatchee?

East Wenatchee's local rate is 0.50%, and the state's price-based rate comes on top of it.

Does Douglas County offer a senior property tax exemption?

Yes, for owners 61 or older, people retired because of a disability, and a veteran with a qualifying disability, depending on household income. Call the Assessor at 509-745-8521.

Who sends the Kitsap County tax bill

Two county offices sit behind your bill. The Treasurer collects the money. The Assessor determines the value that the bill rests on. You can reach both at the Administration Building, 619 Division Street, Port Orchard, through one shared number, (360) 337-5777.

Knowing which desk to call saves time at sale. Take payments, due dates, refunds, delinquent years, excise tax and foreclosure to the Treasurer. Take assessed value, appeals, levy rates and relief programs to the Assessor. The Treasurer's FAQ page follows the same division, and its Parcel Details site shows a tax statement and payment history when you enter an account number or address.

Mail payments to the Kitsap County Treasurer, PO Box 169, Port Orchard WA 98366-0169. Walk-in service at 619 Division Street runs weekdays from 9:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m.

Kitsap County market snapshot

Kitsap County covers the Kitsap Peninsula plus Bainbridge Island, with a long Puget Sound shoreline and many commuters. The cities are Bainbridge Island, Bremerton, Poulsbo and the seat, Port Orchard. Washington State Ferries and Kitsap Transit link the county to Seattle and Edmonds.

  • Owners live in 70.1% of homes (2020-2024 figure).

  • Typical household income: $104,158.

Property tax due dates

Your tax is split into a spring and a fall payment, April 30 and October 31, under RCW 84.56.020. A small bill, $50 or less, is collected all at once on April 30. Statements arrive by mail in February.

The postmark decides whether you are on time. Hand your envelope to a post office clerk on the last day instead of using a drop box. Bank bill-pay can send a paper check by regular mail, so set it up early. A balance still open after October 31 is delinquent, and a parcel you plan to sell should not be in that state at closing.

Homeowners with escrow should know the county does not mail the lender a copy of the statement. Lenders pull account data from the county site. After buying or refinancing, read your escrow statements closely.

What a late payment costs

Unpaid tax accrues interest monthly, at a rate that depends on property type. A home of four or fewer units, manufactured homes included, pays 0.75% per month on the full principal balance and no penalty. Commercial property and residential buildings above four units pay 1% a month, then a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1.

Do not count on forgiveness. The Treasurer grants no good-cause waiver, and a missing statement does not wipe out interest. The exceptions are narrow:

  • The county made an error and never sent the notice.
  • A single missed payment on a personal residence following the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent, provided the Treasurer hears within 60 days of the due date and gets a death certificate.
  • An underpayment caused by an apparent taxpayer error, paid within 30 days of notice.
  • Military owners stationed abroad during an armed conflict.

Paying this year's tax while older years sit open is allowed, though any year that gets three years late can go to foreclosure.

How do I appeal my Kitsap County assessed value?

Appeals go to the Kitsap County Board of Equalization. Counting from the date on your value change notice, you have 60 days, or until July 1 of the assessment year if that is later. Counties may choose that longer window under RCW 84.40.038, and Kitsap does. Notices usually go out in early summer, and the deadline prints on yours. Miss it and you wait a year.

The Board's page explains how a case runs:

  • Filing is free. Each parcel needs its own petition with a copy of the notice attached.
  • The only question is market value on the valuation date, January 1 of the assessment year.
  • Good evidence includes comparable sales close to that date, repair estimates, easement deeds, appraisals and photographs.
  • Hearings run Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., on the fourth floor of the Administration Building or by phone.
  • Decisions usually arrive within two weeks, and state law allows 45 days.

Because the Assessor is presumed right, the proof is your job. If the Board rules against you, the State Board of Tax Appeals will hear a further appeal filed within 30 days of the mailing date. Board phone: 360-337-4424.

Relief programs that matter at sale time

Six programs run through the Assessor, and some affect your numbers at sale: senior and disabled persons exemption and deferral, limited-income homeowner deferral, current use (farm, open space and forest land), residential improvement exemption, destroyed property exemption, and nonprofit exemptions.

The senior and disabled exemption, under RCW 84.36.381, fits owners who have reached 61, who retired because of a disability, or who are a veteran receiving VA compensation at the qualifying rating. The home must be your principal residence, and after a sale the exemption can follow you to a replacement home. Excise tax on a Kitsap County sale

On a sale, the seller pays real estate excise tax before the deed can go to the recorder. Kitsap's local share is 0.50% and the state share is graduated. Pay within 30 days of the date on the conveying document, plus a $5 state technology fee. The Port Orchard counter takes cash or check, and cards add fees.

Both parties sign a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit. Since August 1, 2023, Kitsap also requires that affidavit when it processes a Lack of Probate Affidavit, which matters for inherited homes.   • Up to $551,000 of the selling price: 1.1%.
  • $551,001 to $1,551,000: 1.28%.
  • $1,551,001 to $3,051,000: 2.75%.
  • Above $3,051,000: 3.0%.

Agricultural and timberland keeps a flat 1.28% state rate, and the local rate is added on top. A closing before 2027 uses the older thresholds, so check the exact figure with the Treasurer or your escrow officer.

If property taxes stay unpaid

Foreclosure under chapter 84.64 RCW starts once a tax year is three years late. Paying the at-risk years by the April 30 cutoff halts it.

May is when the county files. Certified mail goes to every party with a recorded interest, and a notice runs in the local paper. Right up to closing time on the final business day before the sale, the owner or any recorded interest holder may redeem by paying all taxes, interest, penalties and costs with certified funds. The county refuses personal checks. After the sale, prior owners lose their rights, except minors and people a court has found incompetent, who have three years to redeem.

The Treasurer's calendar lists a tax foreclosure auction for January 26, 2027 at publicsurplus.com, with January 25, 2027 as the last day to redeem. If older years are delinquent on a home you own, selling before foreclosure is filed is still an option.

Yes. A tax year has to be three years late before foreclosure begins, so a sale before then can clear the balance. The Treasurer can supply a payoff figure for your escrow officer.

Rarely. There is no good-cause waiver. Exceptions cover county error, one missed payment after a close family death, a small taxpayer payment error cured within 30 days, and military owners abroad in an armed conflict.

You get 60 days from your value change notice, or until July 1 if that comes later. Your notice prints the exact date, and the Board at 360-337-4424 can confirm it.

Who handles property tax in Adams County, Washington?

The work is divided. Worth is set by the Assessor, and the Treasurer turns those values into bills and takes the money. Valuation and exemption questions go to the Assessor at 509-659-3200. For what you owe and how to pay, see the Treasurer's office.

Collecting the annual bill is only part of what the Treasurer does. Whenever a property sells, the office acts for the Department of Revenue on the real estate excise tax, and it runs foreclosure against parcels three years in arrears. Statements are meant to reach owners by March 15 under RCW 84.56.020, when levy certifications arrive in time.

Adams County for a property owner

Wheat fields and irrigated crops define this part of eastern Washington. The land covers about 1,925 square miles, and only 11 or so people live on each. Ritzville, where Interstate 90 meets U.S. 395 in the northeast, is the seat. Othello, down in the southwest, is the largest city, with Hatton, Lind and Washtucna as the towns.

For 2025 the estimates are 21,488 people and 7,220 housing units. Across 2020 to 2024 the middle-priced owner-occupied home was worth $273,300, and 69.3 percent of homes had their owners living in them. A great deal of the land is working farm ground, and that affects a sale because agricultural parcels get their own excise tax treatment, described below.

Due dates, interest and liens

One payment by April 30 settles the year. A bill above $50 may instead be split into April 30 and October 31 halves. Late interest follows RCW 84.56.020 and is charged on the full year's tax, not just on the half that was late.

Taxes and excise tax at a sale

January 1 is when the lien for that year's tax begins. The parties can divide the year however the contract says. If it says nothing, RCW 84.60.020 puts the days before the sale on the seller and the days after on the buyer. Escrow instructions normally settle the split, so look at yours.

Every transfer also needs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit. It goes to the Treasurer first, and the deed can be recorded at the Auditor only afterward. Incomplete affidavits are rejected, and forms must be on legal-size paper (8.5 by 14 inches).

  • Payment of excise tax is due 30 days after the sale date, and the Department of Revenue treats the date the deed was notarized as the sale date.
  • Added to the state portion are a local 0.25 percent of the price and a $5 processing fee.
  • State rates climb in steps: 1.1 percent on the first slice, then 1.28, 2.75 and 3.0 percent.
  • A flat state rate of 1.28 percent applies to agricultural or timberland if the buyer will keep it in that use and the Assessor signs the Notice of Continuance on the affidavit.

Farmland is everywhere here, so that last rule is common. Selling wheat ground or an irrigated parcel? Contact the Assessor before closing, not after.

How do you challenge an assessed value?

File a petition with the county board of equalization using a Department of Revenue form. Your deadline under RCW 84.40.038 is whichever comes last: July 1 of the assessment year, 30 days from the mailing or electronic sending of the notice, or a limit the county has adopted of up to 60 days.

The board may excuse lateness when a petition arrives reasonably soon and the owner has good cause. Accepted reasons are a death or serious illness among close family, incorrect written advice from assessor or board staff, a natural disaster, and mail delays the Postal Service can document. The Assessor, at 509-659-3200, can say which deadline applies to your notice.

Senior and disability exemption

The Assessor administers a county exemption for seniors and people with disabilities. Qualifying takes three things: being 61 or older as of December 31 in the application year, living in the home as your principal residence on no more than one acre, and household income of $41,000 or under.

  • State law (RCW 84.36.381) extends eligibility to people retired because of a disability and to recipients of VA compensation rated 40 percent or higher for a service-connected condition.
  • A seller or displaced owner can move the exemption to a replacement home, though only one home per year can claim it.
  • Statements include a note about the state deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.
  • If a mortgage or tax problem is overwhelming, the Washington Homeownership Resource Center answers at 877-894-4663.

What happens when taxes go unpaid for three years?

The Treasurer starts the process. A Certificate of Delinquency is filed with Adams County Superior Court in July, costs begin to pile up, and a title search covers each parcel. People with a recorded interest are notified by certified mail, and the official county newspaper runs a notice as well.

  • A judgment then forecloses the tax lien and authorizes a public auction.
  • Redemption stays open to owners and other interested parties until the end of the business day before the sale.
  • Unsold parcels become Tax Title Property, held by the county in trust. Email the Treasurer for the list.
  • No certificate is filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less, not counting interest and penalties (RCW 84.64.050).

Personal property is handled separately and is not part of a house sale.

Preparing a cash sale of an Adams County property

A sale without a lender follows a schedule you and the buyer choose. Before you list or reply to an offer, take four steps. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff. The whole bill is due April 30, or half on April 30 and half on October 31 if it is over $50. Late amounts accrue interest by the month.

Homes with up to four units pay the lower rate and no penalties, while other property pays a higher yearly rate plus two later penalties. The table above has the figures.

Who pays real estate excise tax when I sell in Adams County?

Normally the seller, though the buyer becomes responsible if the seller fails to pay. The Treasurer takes it with the affidavit, ahead of recording.

How long does Adams County wait before foreclosing for unpaid property tax?

Three full years. A Certificate of Delinquency then goes to Superior Court in July, and you can still redeem before the auction.

Who can I call about the senior exemption in Adams County?

The Assessor's Office, 509-659-3200. Age, residence, acreage and income limits apply, and the section above spells them out.

Who handles Lewis County property tax

Lewis County keeps billing and valuing in separate offices. One sends the bill and takes payment, the Treasurer, and the other, the Assessor, decides what the property is worth. The Treasurer sits in the Historic Courthouse, 351 NW North Street, Chehalis, with a mailing address of PO Box 509, Chehalis, WA 98532. Reach the Treasurer at 360-740-1115. For anything about value, ring the Assessor's Office at 360-740-1392.

Your bill rests on three things: the taxable value from the Assessor, any special-use exemption that lowers it, and the levy rate each taxing district sets under state law. A mortgage company that pays from escrow means no bill comes to you. If you expect a statement and nothing has arrived by mid-March, call the office.

Lewis County in brief

Lewis County is large and mostly rural, strung along the Interstate 5 corridor in Southwest Washington. Chehalis is the seat and Centralia the largest city, with Morton, Mossyrock, Napavine, Toledo, Vader, Winlock and the town of Pe Ell making up the rest. Population was 88,062 in July 2025, up 7.2% since April 2020. Roughly 75.8% of homes are owner-occupied, with a typical value of $385,800 and typical gross rent of $1,097. With just 431 building permits in 2025, new construction rarely competes with a resale here.

Due dates and payment options

The bill splits into an April 30 payment and an October 31 payment. When the whole bill is $50 or less, all of it is due April 30. A weekend October 31 pushes the deadline to the next business day, which in 2026 was Monday, November 2. After the second date, any balance on a parcel you plan to sell is delinquent.

Statements go out around mid-February. The county offers e-statements and ACH payment, which draws the tax from your checking or savings account on the due date. If the bank returns a payment, the payment is voided and a $35 fee is added to any interest and penalty. Mail to the Lewis County Treasurer, PO Box 509, Chehalis, WA 98532, and send it early, since the county judges timeliness by postmark.

Interest begins on the first of the next month and is charged monthly on the unpaid tax. For a residence of up to four units, mobile homes too, the charge is 0.75% a month with no penalty. Everything else pays 1% a month, plus a one-time 3% penalty if unpaid on June 1 and a one-time 8% if unpaid on December 1.

The Treasurer's FAQ offers a practical tip. If you miss April 30, pay the first half plus the interest and penalty built up so far at any time before October 31, and further charges stop.

RCW 84.56.020 adds some protection. A treasurer may offer payment agreements for past due taxes, and an owner who passes the senior income test and lives in the home can seek a waiver of interest and penalties as the three-year mark nears, if the parcel is already in a foreclosure action. Delinquent owners must also be sent the number for the statewide foreclosure hotline.

How do I appeal my Lewis County property value?

Your petition to the Board of Equalization is timely if filed by July 1 of the assessment year, or inside 30 days of the date printed on your value change notice when that is later. The 30-day window is the default in RCW 84.40.038, and Lewis County uses it. Attach a copy of the notice, or the Board treats the petition as incomplete.

A notice reports value as of January 1 for taxes payable the following year, drawn from the prior year's sales. It is not a tax bill. You can file three ways:

  • By mail to the Board of Equalization, 351 NW North St., Room 210, Chehalis, WA 98532.

Every parcel needs its own petition, which asks four things: owner details, the land and improvement values you claim, your specific reasons, and power of attorney if an agent files for you. At least 30 days before the hearing, the Board mails notice. Hearings are held on Thursdays and Fridays, with evidence due 21 business days ahead. You will have a decision within 45 days. Taking it further to the State Board of Tax Appeals must happen within 30 days of the postmark.

The county's guide is blunt about what counts. The question is market value, and comparable sales from the prior year in your area carry the most weight. What your neighbor pays, a percentage jump, hardship and the size of your bill prove nothing about market value. The Assessor's number is presumed correct, which means you must bring clear, cogent and convincing evidence. Staff encourage you to call the Assessor first, since an agreement can let you withdraw the petition.

Land and improvements on your valuation notice

Land and improvements are valued separately, and in Lewis County improvements covers more than the house. Garages, barns and outbuildings, wells, septic systems, utilities and driveways all count. Land is valued as if bare, so trees, vegetation and landscaping stay out of the land figure.

Read that split closely before you list. If a well or septic system is failing, or an outbuilding no longer stands, say so in the petition with photos or a repair estimate, because the form asks for land and improvement values separately. The county also publishes prior-year sales data you can filter by area to build a comparison.

The Assessor's Office, 360-740-1392, runs the main relief program. The county states that an exemption, once granted, does not need to be repaid. A surviving spouse or domestic partner may qualify from age 57 when the other spouse was receiving the exemption.

For owners in the lowest income tier, the statute freezes the valuation used for the exemption at the level of the year you first qualify, and lets you transfer the exemption to a replacement home after a sale. Both income limits and exempt amounts shift for taxes payable in 2027, so get your own figures from the Assessor. If you are denied, a petition to the Board of Equalization is available on its forms page. A tax deferral is different from an exemption, so confirm which one you hold before you sell.

Closing a Lewis County sale

Deeded transfers start with the Treasurer, who handles the real estate excise tax affidavit. Bring four printed copies. Processing costs a $10 minimum per affidavit, and nothing is taken after 4 p.m., so the Auditor has time to record before the day ends.

The state share rises with price. On sales from January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue schedule is 1.1% to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000, then 3.0%. Local rates, listed on the county's REET page, come on top. Sellers normally pay, and unpaid REET can turn into a lien on the property. No. The county says the exemption does not need to be repaid once it is granted. A tax deferral is different, so ask the Assessor which program you hold before you sell.

Both property tax offices are in the Davenport courthouse, 450 Logan Street. The Treasurer collects tax at PO Box 370, Davenport, WA 99122, and answers at 509-725-5061. The Assessor, at PO Box 400, values property and can be reached at 509-725-7011 or 509-596-1454, weekdays, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Here is the valuation rule. The Assessor must set each property at 100% of true and fair market value and must see every property in person at least once in six years. A reappraisal can come earlier, and values may drop when the market does. If you dispute a value, the County Board of Equalization hears it.

The Treasurer takes mailed payments, online payments and payments by phone at 866-898-2915.

Lincoln County market snapshot

Parcels in Lincoln County, a wide and thinly settled place on eastern Washington's Big Bend Plateau, sit far apart. Davenport is the seat and the biggest city, Harrington and Sprague are the other cities, and the towns are Almira, Creston, Odessa, Reardan and Wilbur. With about 2,310 square miles of land and 4.7 people per square mile, it is the fifth-least populous county in Washington.

  • Population in July 2025: 11,982, up 10.1% from April 2020.
  • Housing units: 6,178, with 80.4% owner-occupied.

Few new homes get built, so a well-kept resale faces little local competition from new construction.

Due dates and payment rules

The bill has two fixed dates, April 30 and October 31. A weekend October 31, like the one in 2026, makes the next Monday the deadline, and the Treasurer posts the date. After that, any second-half balance still open is accruing interest.

The mechanics come from RCW 84.56.020. Halves are allowed for bills of $50 or more; anything smaller is due whole on April 30. Mail with an unreadable postmark is still on time if it shows up within three business days of the due date. The treasurer may take partial payments or set up payment agreements, and money for delinquent years is applied to the oldest year first, unless you request otherwise.

Late payment interest and penalties

State law fixes the rates by property type. Residences with up to four units owe nine percent a year, charged monthly, and no penalty. All other real and personal property owes twelve percent a year, with a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty added December 1 of the tax year.

Two more statutory rules may apply to you:

  • A delinquent owner gets a notice with the statewide foreclosure hotline, and at the two-year mark the treasurer hands the owner's name and property address to a homeownership resource center.
  • As the three-year point nears, an owner with limited income who lives in the home may have interest and penalties waived if the parcel is in a foreclosure action. The waiver is available once per property.

Phone 509-725-5061 for a payoff statement before listing the parcel.

Appealing a Lincoln County assessment

Your petition goes to the Board of Equalization clerk. Whichever comes later controls: July 1, or the thirtieth day after your notice was mailed. The 30-day period is the statutory default in RCW 84.40.038. The county's Board page recommends asking the Assessor to re-inspect first, and the Assessor's Office will help you complete the petition form.

The Board's only task is market value on January 1 of the assessment year. You carry the burden of showing the Assessor made an error and that the value is out of line with the market. Comparable sales help most, and so do maps or photographs backing your figure. Arguments about other properties' assessments, the size of an increase, hardship or the amount of tax are off the table.

Timing is tight. The Board needs your evidence at least 21 working days before the hearing. Notice of the hearing usually goes out 22 days ahead, and the decision generally follows within two weeks. Exemptions and programs

Two programs are handled by the Assessor: current use, and the senior citizen and disabled persons exemption. With the exemption, your residence's taxable value is frozen and you are relieved of excess and special levies, and perhaps regular levies as well. Coverage reaches a primary residence plus up to one acre, and a mobile home on rented land can qualify.

Applicants pass an age or disability test and must have owned the home by December 31 of the year before the tax is due. For a 2026 exemption that meant owning by December 31, 2025. Six months of living in the home by that date is required, and if a trust holds title, a copy goes to the Assessor. New medical deductions and a standard deduction have been added, and the thresholds rise under state law for taxes payable in 2027. For today's income limit, call the Assessor rather than relying on an old brochure. A screening tool from the state assessors' association is linked from the county site.

RCW 84.36.381 lets a claimant move the exemption to a replacement residence after selling, which helps if you plan to buy again in the county.

Excise tax when a Lincoln County home sells

Sellers owe Washington's real estate excise tax, and the clock starts on the sale date, not the recording date. In Lincoln County the deed, the affidavit and the check all go to the Treasurer in Davenport. If nobody pays it, the tax can become a lien on the house.

A month's delay brings interest back to the sale date, at 6% for 2026 and 2027. State rates for sales beginning January 1, 2027 step up from 1.1% on the first $551,000 to 1.28% through $1,551,000, 2.75% through $3,051,000 and 3.0% beyond. Classified farm and timber land keeps a flat 1.28% state rate. The Department of Revenue page notes that a local rate is added, so ask the Treasurer which one covers your parcel.

Tax title auctions

A foreclosed parcel that attracts no bid becomes tax title property, which the county sells later. Lincoln County holds its foreclosure and tax title auction in the courthouse lobby at 450 Logan Street, with registration an hour before bidding starts. Minimum bids can be small, and the county's notice shows which parcels are offered and which are withdrawn.

If you own a parcel with years of unpaid tax, call the Treasurer before it reaches this stage. A quick sale to a cash buyer, or any buyer able to close fast, can settle the balance before the county takes the property.

Benton County offices

Value is set by the Assessor and tax is collected by the Treasurer, both county offices. You will find the Assessor's main office at 7122 W. Okanogan Pl., Building E, in Kennewick, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. In Prosser the Assessor sees people by appointment only, Tuesday through Thursday.

  • Assessor: 509-735-2394 (Kennewick) or 509-786-2046 (Prosser). State law calls for every parcel to be valued at 100 percent of fair market value.
  • Treasurer: counters at the Prosser courthouse, 620 Market Street, second floor, and in the Kennewick administration building, suite E110. Forms and payment links are on the Treasurer's property tax page.
  • Board of Equalization: the body that hears valuation appeals, linked from the Assessor's site.

Benton County for a home seller

The Columbia River wraps the north, south and east sides of this south-central Washington county. Prosser holds the county seat while Kennewick has the most people. Richland, West Richland and Benton City are the other cities, and Finley is a census-designated place. Public land, much of it the Hanford Site, takes up roughly a third of the county, and the Red Mountain wine district sits wholly within it.

Residents numbered 206,873 in 2020 and are estimated at 221,722 for 2025. Between 2020 and 2024 the middle owner-occupied home was valued at $407,800, with owners in 67.6 percent of homes. Builders pulled 1,663 permits in 2025, so new construction competes with resale in some neighborhoods.

How to pay Benton County property tax

Options include online, mail, in person and two automatic withdrawal plans. Vendor fees are charged on both online and counter payments.

When are Benton County taxes due?

Settle the year by April 30, or split it into April 30 and October 31 halves. A bill below $50 must be paid whole on April 30. A deadline on a weekend rolls to the next Monday, and a postmark on or before the date makes mail timely.

Both interest and penalty apply to the whole principal balance. RCW 84.56.020 charges a residential parcel of up to four units 9 percent a year without penalties. Everything else owes 12 percent, plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1. Hardship earns no extension, but late payment is not reported to credit agencies.

Local quirks complicate the bill. Assessments from Columbia Irrigation District and Kiona Irrigation District appear on the property tax bill and are paid along with it, which can lead a mortgage servicer to adjust an escrow payment. Benton Irrigation District sends its own bill, due April 1, with no interest or penalty until after April 30. Kennewick Irrigation District collects for itself. Weed control, soil conservation, mosquito control and horticultural pest and disease control charges ride on the bill too, and each creates an enforceable lien.

Who pays what at a Benton County closing?

The tax belongs to the parcel, and foreclosures run against the property itself. A purchaser should find out the tax status before buying, and both parties should agree how the year's tax is treated at closing.

When a contract is silent, RCW 84.60.020 splits the year at the sale date: the seller is responsible for the portion of the calendar year up to the sale, and the buyer for what follows. New-year statements go to the December 1 owner, so pass any statement that reaches you after closing along to the new owner.

  • Have title or escrow pull the tax status ahead of closing.
  • Find out if irrigation or special district charges are included.
  • Real estate excise tax falls due on the sale date no matter when the deed is recorded, and it is normally the seller's cost.
  • To change the taxpayer name legally, file an excise tax affidavit with the Treasurer.

How do you appeal a Benton County valuation?

Speak with the Assessor first. If the value still seems off, petition the Benton County Board of Equalization. RCW 84.40.038 sets the filing deadline at July 1 of the assessment year, 30 days after the notice, or a county limit of up to 60 days, whichever is latest.

A bigger valuation does not by itself mean a bigger bill. Each district's levy is shared among all its properties, so what matters is how your value moved relative to the others. If yours rose faster than your neighbors' did, your share climbs.

Paying under protest to keep a refund claim alive requires following RCW 84.68.020 and WAC 458-18-215. The Treasurer simply files the protest papers and does not rule on whether they are legally adequate.

Tax relief for seniors and disabled owners

An exemption may be available if you are 61 or older, or retired because of a disability, and you own and live in the home. Apply through the Assessor. Participants are excused from voted levies, which make up about 40 percent of an average Benton County tax bill. Seniors can also defer, letting the estate pay later.

On the Assessor's forms page you will find the exemption application, deferral applications for seniors and for limited-income homeowners, and an exemption for physical improvements to a single family home. Keep paying while your application is pending. Only the Assessor's approval lets the Treasurer change the amount due, and a refund or revised bill follows.

When does Benton County foreclose for unpaid taxes?

Three full years of delinquency open the door to real property foreclosure. It starts in June and finishes with a sale in November, and money beyond the taxes and costs goes back to the former owner. Personal property is collected the moment it turns delinquent. Notice is published in a local newspaper's legal column.

Near that point? Selling before a case is filed preserves your equity. A cash buyer can settle with the Treasurer out of the proceeds and give you what is left.

Frequently asked questions

When are property taxes due in Benton County, WA?

The first half, or the full year, on April 30, and the second half on October 31. Weekend dates move to Monday, and small bills under $50 are due whole in April.

Can I pay Benton County property tax by credit card?

Yes. Credit cards and non-Visa debit cards carry a 2.5 percent vendor fee, e-check costs $1, and Visa debit costs $3.95 a transaction. Counter payments pay the same fees.

How can I spread Benton County property tax over the year?

Sign up for the monthly installment plan: nine withdrawals on the 15th at $0.75 each, with applications due January 5 for the first half or May 1 for the second. The semi-annual ACH plan pulls money in April and October for free.

Who owes the tax when a Benton County house sells mid-year?

By default under RCW 84.60.020, the seller covers the time before the sale date and the buyer the time after. Work out the split in escrow and verify the balance with the Treasurer.

Can I appeal my Benton County property tax bill?

Yes, through a petition to the Board of Equalization asking for a lower assessed value. Timing is July 1, 30 days from the notice, or up to 60 days if the county has set that limit, whichever is latest.

Stevens County offices and phone numbers

Two county officers handle the tax, and a third clerk handles appeals. Statements and payments run through the Treasurer. Parcel values come from the Assessor. Both sit in the courthouse at 215 S Oak St in Colville.

  • Treasurer: Room 103, 509-684-2593, open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. Email goes to treasurer@stevenscountywa.gov.
  • Assessor: Room 101, 509-684-6161, open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. until 4 p.m. This office also runs exemptions and current use classification.
  • Board of Equalization clerk: 230 E. Birch St in the Commissioner's building, 509-684-7513. Hours are limited, so email ahead for an appointment.

Before you list a house, those three contacts can answer nearly every tax question that will come up at closing.

Stevens County housing at a glance

Stevens County is big, quiet country on the Canadian line in northeastern Washington. Colville is the county seat and largest town, and it is part of the Spokane metro area. The county had 49,668 residents in July 2025, spread over 2,477 square miles of land, so most parcels outside Colville are rural.

  • Share of homes that are owner-occupied: 79.8 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Typical value of a home lived in by its owner: $350,600.
  • Median household income: $69,327.
  • Residents 65 and over: 27.8 percent.

With more than a quarter of residents past 65, many owners here are candidates for the senior exemption and the deferral program covered below.

When are Stevens County property taxes due?

Half is owed by April 30 and the other half by October 31, a split that RCW 84.56.020 permits once your total reaches $50. Smaller bills go in a single April payment. On mailed checks the Post Office cancellation mark rules, and a date from a postage meter is ignored.

You can pay at the counter, by mail, in the drop box outside the Treasurer's office, in the drive-up box behind the courthouse, or by card through the county's payment vendor, which adds its own fee. A returned check costs $25 and voids the payment for that parcel.

If you are unsure what is still open on your parcel, call 509-684-2593.

Unpaid tax and foreclosure

Interest begins on the delinquency date. A house can go to tax foreclosure once the oldest tax is three full years behind. On houses and other residential property of four units or fewer, RCW 84.56.020 sets interest at 9 percent yearly, with penalties reserved for other property types. A written figure from the Treasurer beats any estimate.

The county runs its foreclosure sale online. The next sale is scheduled for December 4, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. and covers parcels whose 2023 tax is still unpaid. For an owner, the process breaks down like this:

  • Redemption stays open until the close of business on the day before the auction.
  • Real property tax holds first lien position, so a foreclosure can wipe out a deed of trust, mortgage or judgment. Local improvement district assessments and IRS liens stay with the property.
  • A parcel nobody bids on becomes tax title property held by the county.
  • A title search on each foreclosure parcel costs about $350, and that cost is added to the redemption amount.

An income-qualified owner who lives in a home in foreclosure can have interest and penalties waived, once, if the Assessor verifies eligibility. If you are behind and want to sell ahead of the sale date, call 509-684-2593 for the redemption total and pass that number to your escrow officer.

How do you appeal a Stevens County assessment?

Your petition to the county Board of Equalization is due July 1 of the assessment year, unless the window after your value notice was mailed runs longer. The county counts 30 days from the mailing date on the Assessor's change of value notice. RCW 84.40.038 lets a county adopt a limit as long as 60 days. The deadline printed on your own notice controls, and the clerk can clear up any mismatch.

Three private citizens sit on the board, with up to four alternates, all appointed by the county commissioners. The board also hears denials of senior and disabled exemptions, current use decisions and forest land classifications.

  • Give the Assessor a duplicate of each paper you submit.
  • A faxed or emailed petition protects the deadline only. The signed original has to follow.
  • A missed deadline can sometimes be rescued with a late-filing request under WAC 458-14-056, so contact the clerk quickly.

Keep paying your tax on schedule while an appeal is open. Any change in value shows up later as a lower bill or a refund.

Tax relief for homeowners

The county Assessor runs Washington's senior and disability exemption. To get it, you must own and live in the home as your primary residence, have qualifying income, and by December 31 of the assessment year meet one of these tests:

  • Age 61 or older.
  • At least 57 and the surviving spouse or domestic partner of someone who was in the program.
  • Disabled and unable to work, whatever your age.
  • A service-connected disability rating of at least 40 percent, or compensation at the 100 percent rate.

Each county sets its own income ceiling. Call the Stevens County Assessor at 509-684-6161 for the current limit and an application. The office keeps income and expense details from these applications confidential.

A separate state deferral program pays the tax for you and takes a lien on the house. The deferred tax plus interest must be repaid once you stop owning and living in the home, which means a sale puts that lien into closing. Get the payoff from the Assessor early.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Stevens County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How is property tax handled when you sell a Stevens County house?

Unless the contract says something else, the year's tax is split by days of ownership. RCW 84.60.020 has the lien attach on January 1, and when a contract is silent the seller carries the months before the sale date while the buyer carries the months after.

In practice, escrow asks the Treasurer where both halves stand, takes your share from proceeds and pays anything open. Before listing, or before you say yes to an offer, work through three checks:

  • Search the parcel on the Stevens County property search and see what is paid.
  • Ask the Treasurer if an earlier year is delinquent, since a clean current year does not wipe out an older balance.
  • Ask the Assessor whether an exemption, a deferral or a current use classification sits on the parcel, and what ending it would cost.

What a closing looks like when taxes are involved

A typical sale in Colville runs in a few steps. You sign a purchase contract, escrow opens, and the escrow officer orders a tax status from the Treasurer. If a prior year is open, the payoff gets added to your closing statement. If a deferral or exemption is attached, the Assessor's payoff or removal notice goes in the file too.

A cash buyer skips the lender's underwriting, so there is less back and forth over escrow accounts, though the title company still checks the tax record. Whatever is owed leaves your proceeds before the deed records, and the buyer takes the property with the current year in order. Bring your latest tax statement and the parcel number to your first meeting with escrow, and mention any foreclosure notice or payment arrangement right away.

Frequently asked questions

When is the second half of Stevens County property tax due?

October 31 each year, judged by postmark on mailed payments. If the date falls on a weekend, ask the Treasurer at 509-684-2593 about the deadline and your open balance.

Can I pay Stevens County property tax in two halves?

Yes, once your total hits $50. Pay one half in spring and the other in fall. A total under $50 has no second installment and is paid in one go by April 30.

How long can Stevens County property tax go unpaid before foreclosure?

Three full years. The sale set for December 4, 2026 covers parcels with the 2023 tax year unpaid, and an owner can redeem until the business day before the sale.

How do I appeal my Stevens County property value?

File a petition with the Board of Equalization by July 1 or by the date tied to your notice mailing, which the county sets at 30 days. Call the clerk at 509-684-7513 and send the Assessor a copy.

Does a sale clear the property tax lien in Stevens County?

Escrow subtracts any back tax from your net at the closing table. Because the lien attaches each January 1, the escrow officer confirms the current share and any delinquent year with the Treasurer before the deed records.
